+class _Qwen4ExpPreparedRotaryEmbedding(torch.nn.Module):
+    """Consume prepared RoPE rows without replacing upstream QKV projection."""
+
+    def __init__(self, delegate: torch.nn.Module) -> None:
+        super().__init__()
+        self.delegate = delegate
+        self._prepared_cos_sin: torch.Tensor | None = None
+
+    def __getattr__(self, name: str) -> Any:
+        try:
+            return super().__getattr__(name)
+        except AttributeError:
+            delegate = super().__getattr__("delegate")
+            return getattr(delegate, name)
+
+    def set_prepared_cos_sin(self, cos_sin: torch.Tensor) -> None:
+        self._prepared_cos_sin = cos_sin
+
+    def _can_use_prepared(
+        self,
+        positions: torch.Tensor,
+        query: torch.Tensor,
+        key: torch.Tensor | None,
+        offsets: torch.Tensor | None,
+    ) -> bool:
+        from vllm.triton_utils import HAS_TRITON
+
+        prepared = self._prepared_cos_sin
+        if not HAS_TRITON or prepared is None or key is None or offsets is not None:
+            return False
+        if positions.ndim not in (1, 2):
+            return False
+        if positions.ndim == 2 and (
+            not getattr(self.delegate, "mrope_interleaved", False)
+            or getattr(self.delegate, "mrope_section", None) is None
+        ):
+            return False
+        expected_shape = (*positions.shape, self.delegate.cos_sin_cache.shape[-1])
+        num_tokens = positions.shape[-1]
+        return bool(
+            tuple(prepared.shape) == expected_shape
+            and prepared.device == query.device
+            and prepared.dtype == query.dtype
+            and key.device == query.device
+            and key.dtype == query.dtype
+            and query.shape[0] == num_tokens
+            and key.shape[0] == num_tokens
+        )
+
+    def _forward_prepared(
+        self,
+        positions: torch.Tensor,
+        query: torch.Tensor,
+        key: torch.Tensor,
+    ) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+        prepared = self._prepared_cos_sin
+        if prepared is None:
+            raise RuntimeError("Qwen4Exp prepared RoPE rows are unavailable")
+        cos, sin = prepared.chunk(2, dim=-1)
+        query_shape = query.shape
+        key_shape = key.shape
+        if positions.ndim == 2:
+            from vllm.model_executor.layers.rotary_embedding.mrope import triton_mrope
+
+            query, key = triton_mrope(
+                query,
+                key,
+                cos.contiguous(),
+                sin.contiguous(),
+                self.delegate.mrope_section,
+                self.delegate.head_size,
+                self.delegate.rotary_dim,
+                self.delegate.mrope_interleaved,
+                self.delegate.is_neox_style,
+            )
+        else:
+            from vllm_ascend.ops.triton.rope import rope_forward_triton
+
+            num_tokens = positions.shape[0]
+            query, key = rope_forward_triton(
+                query.view(num_tokens, -1, self.delegate.head_size),
+                key.view(num_tokens, -1, self.delegate.head_size),
+                cos=cos,
+                sin=sin,
+                rope_dim=self.delegate.rotary_dim,
+                is_neox_style=self.delegate.is_neox_style,
+            )
+        return query.reshape(query_shape), key.reshape(key_shape)
+
+    def forward(
+        self,
+        positions: torch.Tensor,
+        query: torch.Tensor,
+        key: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+        offsets: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+    ) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor | None]:
+        if self._can_use_prepared(positions, query, key, offsets):
+            if key is None:
+                raise RuntimeError("Qwen4Exp prepared RoPE requires a key tensor")
+            return self._forward_prepared(positions, query, key)
+        if offsets is None:
+            return self.delegate(positions, query, key)
+        return self.delegate(positions, query, key, offsets)
+
+
+class Qwen4ExpPreparedInputAdapter:
+    """Prepare model-specific replay inputs without changing public MRV2."""
+
+    def __init__(self, model: torch.nn.Module) -> None:

+            module for module in model.modules() if module.__class__.__name__ == "AscendQwen4ExpQSAAttention"
+        )

+        self._metadata_buffers: dict[tuple[object, ...], torch.Tensor] = {}

+                not layer.layer_name.startswith("mtp.")
+                and isinstance(rotary, torch.nn.Module)

+    def prepare_inputs(self, input_batch: Any) -> None:

+        self.prepare_positions(
+            input_batch.positions,
+            input_batch.num_tokens_after_padding,
+        )
+
+    def prepare_positions(self, positions: torch.Tensor, num_tokens: int) -> None:
+        """Prepare one- or three-axis MRoPE positions for capture/replay."""
+        if positions.ndim == 1:
+            positions = positions[:num_tokens]
+        elif positions.ndim == 2:
+            positions = positions[:, :num_tokens]
+        else:
+            raise ValueError("QSA positions must be one- or two-dimensional")

+        for layer in self._layers:
+            if layer.layer_name.startswith("mtp."):

+            cache_key = (
+                cache.data_ptr(),
+                tuple(positions.shape),
+                layer.q_norm.weight.dtype,
+                layer.q_norm.weight.device,
+            )
+            prepared = prepared_by_cache.get(cache_key)
+            if prepared is not None:
+                if isinstance(layer.rotary_emb, _Qwen4ExpPreparedRotaryEmbedding):

+                self._rope_buffers[key] = buffer

+            if isinstance(layer.rotary_emb, _Qwen4ExpPreparedRotaryEmbedding):

+            else:

+        self,

+    def _persistent_metadata(
+        self,
+        signature: tuple[object, ...],

+    def _prepare_lightning(
+        self,
+        layer: Any,
+        metadata: Any,
+        *,
+        full_graph: bool,
+        prepared_this_step: dict[tuple[object, ...], torch.Tensor],
+    ) -> None:

+            _tensor_storage_signature(query_start_loc),

+        )

+            signature,
+            generated,
+        )
+        prepared_this_step[signature] = metadata.qsa_lightning_v2_metadata
+
+    def _prepare_gbsa(
+        self,
+        layer: Any,
+        main: Any,
+        raw: Any,
+        *,

+    The QSA producer must provide packed, contiguous query suffixes: local row i
+    of request r has logical position seq_lens[r] - query_len[r] + i. The upstream
+    QSA builder establishes this relationship. Request boundaries start at zero
+    and their final live boundary equals the number of live query rows. Positions
+    and token_to_req must describe those same rows; arbitrary reordering is not
+    supported. These are value-level preconditions, not host tensor reads here.
+
+    Optional host counts trim graph-padding requests/rows before V2. Supply
+    them from existing CPU scheduling metadata, not by reading NPU tensors.
+    Without counts, all input rows and requests are assumed live. Live requests
+    and rows must occupy contiguous prefixes of the corresponding inputs.
+
+    Preserve the original [query_rows,2051] INT32 output ABI, including the
+    caller's buffer identity. The first 515 columns hold 512 logical group IDs

+    Later MTP steps must continue to reuse the buffer without invoking selection.

+    # CANN checks even singleton-axis strides strictly. Cache views may have

+    # preserving storage, storage offset and the physical stride between pages.
+    compressed_key_cache = canonicalize_singleton_dim_strides(compressed_key_cache)
+    if token_topk != _TOKEN_TOPK or compress_ratio != _COMPRESS_RATIO:
+        raise ValueError("QSA LI V2 requires token_topk=2048 and compress_ratio=4")
+    rows = query.shape[0]
+    requests = sequence_lengths.shape[0] if num_actual_requests is None else num_actual_requests

+        raise ValueError("QSA LI V2 metadata does not cover the live requests")
+    if live_rows and not requests:
+        raise ValueError("QSA LI V2 nonempty queries require live requests")
+    # These packing inputs and the caller's output do not go through CANN.
+    if token_to_req.shape != (rows,) or query_positions.shape != (rows,):
+        raise ValueError("QSA LI V2 row metadata must match query rows")
+    if any(t.device != query.device for t in (token_to_req, query_positions, sequence_lengths)):
+        raise ValueError("QSA packing metadata must be on the query device")
+    if any(t.dtype not in (torch.int32, torch.int64) for t in (token_to_req, query_positions)):
+        raise ValueError("QSA row mappings and positions must be integer tensors")
+    output_width = token_topk + compress_ratio - 1
+    if out is not None and (
+        out.shape != (rows, output_width) or out.dtype != torch.int32 or out.device != query.device
+    ):
+        raise ValueError("QSA LI V2 output must match query rows, INT32 dtype and device")
+    if out is None:
+        out = torch.empty((rows, output_width), dtype=torch.int32, device=query.device)
+    out.fill_(-1)
+    if not live_rows:
+        return out
+
+    # Metadata uses original-token lengths. Only these two request-sized arrays
+    # are materialized; there is no token-wise length or page-table gather.
+    lengths = sequence_lengths[:requests]
+    compressed_lengths = lengths.floor_divide(compress_ratio)
+    residual_lengths = lengths.remainder(compress_ratio)
+    common = dict(
+        cu_seqlens_q=query_start_loc[: requests + 1],
+        seqused_k=compressed_lengths,
+        cmp_residual_k=residual_lengths,
+        layout_q="TND",
+        layout_k="PA_BBND",
+        mask_mode=3,
+        cmp_ratio=compress_ratio,
+    )
+    block_topk = token_topk // compress_ratio
+    metadata = prepared_metadata
+    if metadata is None:
+        metadata = lightning_indexer_v2_metadata(
+            query.shape[1],
+            1,
+            _HEAD_DIM,
+            block_topk,
+            batch_size=requests,
+            **common,
+        )
+    # Promote the old BF16-representable uniform weight to FP32. Keep its
+    # effective value while removing zero-head padding supported by native V2.
+    score_weight = math.ldexp(
+        round(math.ldexp(1.0 / math.sqrt(_HEAD_DIM), _LI_V2_WEIGHT_FRACTION_BITS)),
+        -_LI_V2_WEIGHT_FRACTION_BITS,
+    )
+    weights = torch.full(
+        (live_rows, query.shape[1]),
+        score_weight,
+        dtype=torch.float32,
+        device=query.device,
+    )
+    groups, _ = lightning_indexer_v2(
+        query[:live_rows],
+        compressed_key_cache,
+        weights,
+        block_topk,
+        block_table=block_table[:requests],
+        metadata=metadata,
+        return_value=0,
+        **common,
+    )
+    packed_width = block_topk + compress_ratio - 1
+    pack_qsa_group_indices_npu(
+        groups.squeeze(1),
+        query_positions[:live_rows],
+        lengths,
+        token_to_req[:live_rows],
+        compress_ratio,
+        token_topk,
+        out[:live_rows, :packed_width],
+    )
+    return out

[Refactor][KV Pool] Refactor layerwise KV pooling into data-plane strategies (#21314)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Isolate the plane-specific logic of the layerwise AscendStore KV pool
behind an explicit data-plane interface, deduplicate the idioms both
backend protocols had re-implemented, and delete two generations of
unreachable legacy transfer paths. Net: 21 files, +1255/−1698. No
behavior change is intended: the block-key session protocols and the GVA
protocol bodies were moved verbatim (verified by normalized diff against
the pre-move code), wire-key string formats are unchanged (byte-for-byte
assertions in tests), and the full UT pass/fail set is identical to the
upstream/main baseline — checked after every commit of the original
series, and re-verified at the rebased head against the new baseline.

Note: this series was rebased onto current main after #21949 (DS4.1
shared KV reusing the GVA layerwise path) landed. The rebase keeps that
commit's worker-side additions intact on the worker and carries its
load-lease improvements (per-step lease dedup, and pinned-GVA refresh on
every occurrence of a repeated key) into the moved plane code with the
same `self.` → `worker.` rebinds, so the plane owns upstream's current
lease semantics.

## Why this refactor

Before this series, the layerwise worker carried both backend protocols
inline behind `use_block_key_layerwise` / `use_layerwise_transfer`
flags, which had three costs:

- **Protocol detail leaked into every step method.** Mooncake's session
handling (put/get sessions, revocation, retry release) and memcache's
GVA target preparation (batch_alloc, read leases, partial-key
repointing) shared method bodies, so every transfer-path function had to
reason about which protocol it was currently in. The Mooncake session
functions were module-level helpers with no interface shape at all.
- **Safety-relevant reasoning was duplicated.** The contiguous-hit scan,
the fail-open existence-probe policy, partial-key construction, and
pool-hit/save-start clamping each existed in plane-specific copies that
could drift — and a drift in any of them is a correctness bug, not a
style issue.
- **Dead protocol paths.** Two generations of unreachable entries were
still present: the Key-layer transfer threads, and the older
generator-era `retrieve_layer`/`store_layer` entries with their
`get_event` signal. They imply a third transfer protocol that can never
run.

## Design: a two-hook data plane

`LayerwiseDataPlane` (new `layerwise/planes/`) is a step-level interface
with exactly two hooks, because those are the only two points where the
protocols must diverge at step granularity:

```
store_masks → prepare_sessions → save loop → _build_shared_save_data
            → load loop → _build_shared_load_data
            finish_sessions at load completion / abort
```

- **`prepare_sessions`**: each plane opens its pool sessions and/or
resolves transfer targets here, holding its own ordering invariants. For
the GVA plane the load-before-save order is a protocol invariant — load
preparation queries the GVA registered by the *previous* step's
snapshot, so it must complete before save allocation repoints the
partial key at a fresh one — so it lives (documented) inside the plane
instead of the shared timeline. The fold is behavior-neutral: save-loop
planning is a pure function of pre-step request state and reads no
GVA-pair output, the pair reads no planning output, and the one crossing
(allocation failure setting `can_save = False`) converges to the same
empty save set in both orders.
`test_layerwise_load_is_prepared_before_next_save_allocation` locks the
internal `["load", "save"]` order unchanged.
- **`finish_sessions`**: releases the step's pool-side load sessions.
The GVA plane is a no-op because GVA loads read through worker-held
addresses — the only remaining no-op, and it is the *behavior*
difference, not interface noise.

Earlier revisions of this series exposed three (originally four) hooks;
folding the GVA window into `prepare_sessions` removed the last no-op
stub and the last protocol-specific concept from the interface, so the
upper layer no longer sees GVA vs block-key at step level.

The worker keeps the genuinely shared machinery (key construction, store
I/O batching, session tracking, failure recording, the save-disable
circuit breaker) and drives the timeline through the interface; planes
resolve worker helpers at call time instead of caching bound methods, so
a helper swap keeps affecting the whole step. Backends declare their
plane as a class attribute (`memcache: "gva"`, `mooncake: "block_key"`)
and a factory binds it at config time.

## Detailed changes

- **`layerwise/planes/` (new)**: `BlockKeyDataPlane` owns both block-key
session protocols (single-group and hybrid multi-group, moved verbatim);
`GvaDataPlane` owns the GVA protocol (save-side GVA allocation,
load-side lease/GVA resolution, moved verbatim from the worker).
`backend/mooncake_layerwise.py` shrinks to the wire-key and
layout-identity helpers — those stay in `backend/` because the scheduler
consumes them too.
- **Fold the GVA hooks into the plane** (was `prepare_load_gvas` +
`alloc_save_gvas` as two worker-driven timeline calls, then one
`prepare_gvas` hook; now inside `prepare_sessions`): the pair was always
a single window with a fixed internal order; keeping it on the timeline
exposed a GVA-specific concept through the interface and left a no-op on
the block-key side. The method bodies moved with them into
`planes/gva.py` (verbatim; shared machinery is still reached through
`self._worker`), so the GVA protocol now lives where its name says.
- **Rename `_scan_contiguous_group_hits` →
`_query_contiguous_group_hits`**: it probes the backend per block and
returns one contiguous hit run per participating group; the verb now
matches the `_query_layerwise_block_hits` helper it drives.
- **Share `LoadSpec.pool_hit_tokens` / `LoadSpec.clamp_save_start`**:
identical token-resolution and clamping reasoning existed in both planes
and the worker.
- **Unified existence probes** (`_probe_pool_missing_keys`,
`_filter_pool_existing_keys`): the fail-open policy is deliberate (an
unreadable pool costs hits; a bogus skip costs the blocks themselves),
so it is defined once and cannot drift.
- **`LayerwiseKeyBuilder` owns partial-key construction** (dead
`make_hit_check_keys` shims dropped): the key format is wire protocol
and needs a single point of truth.
- **Delete unreachable legacy paths**: the Key-layer threads
(`KVCacheStoreKeyLayerSendingThread` / `RecvingThread` + their test
class) — `LayerwiseKVPoolWorker` is only constructed with
`use_layerwise`, where the scheduler rejects any data plane other than
`block_key` / `gva` at startup, and the non-layerwise deployment uses
`KVPoolWorker`, which never had them; the generator-era `retrieve_layer`
/ `store_layer`, their payload type `LayerMultiBlockReqMeta` and the
`get_event` shadow signal — the only waiter was `retrieve_layer` itself,
while the current protocol synchronizes on per-layer
`layer_load_finished_events`, so the recving thread kept setting a
signal nobody waited on; `_async_load_enabled` (constant `False`, no
callers, no base-class slot).
- **Drop one-line forwarders**:
`_finish_current_layerwise_load_sessions` (the hybrid rollback path even
bounced plane → worker → plane) and `_make_mooncake_layerwise_key` (a
group-0 forwarder; the hybrid path already called
`_make_layerwise_full_key` directly, so all block-key sites now use one
spelling). Pure indirection hides the real call target.
- **Drop the recving thread's dead failure-policy knob**:
`raise_on_transfer_failure` was declared and stored on the recv side but
never read — load failures already carry their own per-block /
per-request semantics (invalid-block marking, failed-request reporting,
the load abort event). The sending thread keeps the flag; its save path
genuinely reads it.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. This is an internal refactor of the KV transfer and pooling logic:
wire-key string formats, the user-facing config knobs
(`layerwise_max_transfer_blocks`, `layerwise_max_transfer_bytes`,
`h2d_stagger_us`) and all deployment behavior are unchanged, so no
release-note fragment is added.

### How was this patch tested?

- `tests/ut/distributed/ascend_store`: the full-suite pass/fail set is
identical to the upstream/main baseline — checked after every commit of
the original series and re-verified at the rebased head (the single
passing-test delta is the test of the deleted dead dataclass).
- `test_layerwise_load_is_prepared_before_next_save_allocation` passes
explicitly, locking the GVA internal order through `process_layer_data`.
- Block-key session protocols and GVA protocol bodies moved verbatim
(normalized diff); wire-key formats unchanged (byte-for-byte test
assertions).
- Performance no-regression check with AISBench (prefix-cache workload)
on 8 Ascend 905PR cards in a PD-disaggregated deployment (prefill 4 /
decode 4, both DP=4 / TP=1): `python3 aisbench_test.py --input_len
131072 --prefix_num 16 --output_len 1024 --data_num 64 --concurrency 16
--request_rate 0 --dataset_type prefix_cache --repeat_rate 90%
--prefix_test`. Baseline runs use upstream main; candidate runs use this
PR branch. The external hit rate is identical in all four runs (93.72%):

| backend | TTFT avg (ms) | TPOT avg (ms) | E2E throughput (tok/s) |
external_hit_rate |

93.72% |
  | memcache, baseline | 7502.4 | 118.5 | 16074 | 93.72% |
| memcache, + this PR | 8047.2 (+7.3%) | 115.8 (-2.3%) | 16445 (+2.3%) |
93.72% |

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

+
+"""Data-plane strategies for layerwise KV pooling.
+
+The layerwise worker drives every backend plane (block-key, GVA) through one
+interface: pool-session preparation before the per-layer transfer loop, GVA
+target preparation after it, and load-session cleanup at the step boundary.
+The plane implementations own the plane-specific protocol; the worker keeps
+the shared machinery (key construction, store I/O helpers, session tracking)
+both planes call back into.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
+
+from vllm_ascend.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_pool.ascend_store.layerwise.planes.base import (
+    LayerwiseDataPlane,
+)
+from vllm_ascend.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_pool.ascend_store.layerwise.planes.block_key import (
+    BlockKeyDataPlane,
+)
+from vllm_ascend.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_pool.ascend_store.layerwise.planes.gva import (
+    GvaDataPlane,
+)
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from vllm_ascend.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_pool.ascend_store.layerwise.pool_worker import (
+        LayerwiseKVPoolWorker,
+    )
+
+__all__ = [
+    "BlockKeyDataPlane",
+    "GvaDataPlane",
+    "LayerwiseDataPlane",
+    "make_data_plane",
+]
+
+
+def make_data_plane(worker: LayerwiseKVPoolWorker) -> LayerwiseDataPlane:
+    """Bind the data-plane strategy matching the selected backend."""
+    plane = worker.layerwise_data_plane
+    if plane == "block_key":
+        return BlockKeyDataPlane(worker)
+    if plane == "gva":

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+
+"""The layerwise data-plane interface implemented by every backend plane."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from vllm_ascend.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_pool.ascend_store.metadata import ReqMeta
+
+
+class LayerwiseDataPlane(ABC):
+    """Step-level protocol for one layerwise backend data plane.
+
+    The layerwise worker delegates the plane-specific parts of a transfer
+    step to this interface and keeps the shared machinery (key construction,
+    store I/O helpers, session tracking) on itself. Implementations hold a
+    worker reference and must resolve worker helpers at call time instead of
+    caching bound methods, so swapping a helper keeps affecting the whole
+    step.
+    """
+
+    @abstractmethod
+    def prepare_sessions(self, requests: list[ReqMeta]) -> dict[int, list[ReqMeta]]:
+        """Prepare the step's transfers before the per-layer save loop.
+
+        Implementations open pool sessions and/or resolve backend transfer
+        targets here, holding their own internal ordering invariants.
+        Returns the per-group request views the save/load loops consume; an
+        empty dict means the loops keep the requests unchanged.
+        """
+
+    @abstractmethod
+    def finish_sessions(self) -> None:
+        """Release the step's pool-side load sessions."""

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+
+"""Block-key plane: the pool stores one addressable object per block.
+
+Two session protocols live here, both ending in the same worker store I/O:
+
+* Single group (``block_key_hybrid`` unset): one group, one hash-addressed
+  object per block plus a request-scoped trailing partial-block key. The
+  requests themselves carry the session slots.
+* Hybrid (multi-group): per-group request views isolate each group's key
+  slots while preserving real request ownership; only complete blocks are
+  published, and reachability masks gate both load and save entries.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from copy import copy
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
+
+from vllm.logger import logger
+
+from vllm_ascend.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_pool.ascend_store.layerwise.planes.base import (
+    LayerwiseDataPlane,
+)
+from vllm_ascend.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_pool.ascend_store.metadata import (
+    ReqMeta,
+    block_hash_to_str,
+    get_block_hashes,
+)
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from vllm_ascend.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_pool.ascend_store.layerwise.pool_worker import (
+        LayerwiseKVPoolWorker,
+    )
+
+
+def selected(mask, index: int) -> bool:
+    return mask is None or (0 <= index < len(mask) and bool(mask[index]))
+
+
+class BlockKeyDataPlane(LayerwiseDataPlane):
+    """Session bookkeeping for backends addressing one object per block."""
+
+    def __init__(self, worker: LayerwiseKVPoolWorker):
+        self._worker = worker
+
+    # --- step entry points -----------------------------------------------------
+
+    def prepare_sessions(self, requests: list[ReqMeta]) -> dict[int, list[ReqMeta]]:
+        worker = self._worker
+        if worker.block_key_hybrid:
+            return self._prepare_hybrid_sessions(requests)
+        self._prepare_single_group_sessions(requests)
+        return {}
+
+    def finish_sessions(self) -> None:
+        worker = self._worker
+        if worker._layer_load_aborted.is_set():
+            req_ids = worker._current_layerwise_request_ids.copy()
+            worker._release_layerwise_requests_for_retry(req_ids)
+        else:
+            req_ids = worker._current_layerwise_last_chunk_req_ids.copy()
+            worker._release_layerwise_requests_terminal(req_ids)
+        worker._current_layerwise_request_ids.difference_update(req_ids)
+        worker._current_layerwise_last_chunk_req_ids.difference_update(req_ids)
+
+    # --- single-group protocol ---------------------------------------------------
+
+    def _prepare_single_group_sessions(self, requests: list[ReqMeta]) -> None:
+        worker = self._worker
+        worker._layer_load_aborted.clear()
+        worker._current_layerwise_request_ids = {request.req_id for request in requests}
+        worker._current_layerwise_last_chunk_req_ids = {request.req_id for request in requests if request.is_last_chunk}
+        get_key_slots: list[tuple[ReqMeta, str, int, int | None]] = []
+        for request in requests:
+            get_key_slots.extend(
+                (request, key, block_id, slot) for key, block_id, slot in self._prepare_single_get_session(request)
+            )
+        worker._open_layerwise_get_sessions(get_key_slots)
+        for request in requests:
+            self._prepare_single_put_session(request)
+
+    def _prepare_single_put_session(self, request: ReqMeta) -> None:
+        worker = self._worker
+        request.save_block_keys = []
+        request.save_last_block_key = None
+        if not worker._is_layerwise_save_owner() or not request.can_save:
+            return
+
+        start_block = request.save_start_token // worker.block_size
+        end_block = request.save_end_token // worker.block_size
+        if request.load_spec is not None:
+            start_block = request.load_spec.clamp_save_start(start_block, worker.block_size)
+        group_block_hashes = get_block_hashes(request.block_hashes, worker.block_size, worker.hash_block_size)
+        request.save_key_block_offset = start_block
+        request.save_block_keys = [None] * max(0, end_block - start_block)
+        key_slots: list[tuple[str, int | None, int]] = []
+        for block_index in range(start_block, min(end_block, len(group_block_hashes))):
+            key = worker._make_layerwise_full_key(0, block_hash_to_str(group_block_hashes[block_index]))
+            request.save_block_keys[block_index - start_block] = key
+            key_slots.append((key, block_index - start_block, block_index))
+
+        if request.partial_block_index is not None:
+            request.save_last_block_key = worker._make_layerwise_full_key(0, f"{request.req_id}_lastblock")
+            key_slots.append((request.save_last_block_key, None, request.partial_block_index))
+
+        requested_keys = list(dict.fromkeys(key for key, _, _ in key_slots))
+        if not requested_keys:
+            return
+        with worker._put_started_keys_lock:
+            previously_started = set(requested_keys) & worker._put_started_keys
+            new_keys = [key for key in requested_keys if key not in worker._put_started_keys]
+
+        started = set(previously_started)
+        if new_keys:
+            try:
+                results = worker._start_layerwise_put_keys(new_keys, worker._layerwise_object_size_bytes())
+            except Exception as exc:
+                logger.error("Layerwise batch_put_start failed keys=%s error=%s", new_keys, exc)
+                with worker._put_started_keys_lock:
+                    worker._put_started_keys.update(new_keys)
+                worker._queue_layerwise_revoke_keys(new_keys)
+            else:
+                newly_started = {key for key, result in zip(new_keys, results, strict=True) if result == 0}
+                with worker._put_started_keys_lock:
+                    worker._put_started_keys.update(newly_started)
+                started.update(newly_started)
+
+        for key, slot, _ in key_slots:
+            if key in started:
+                if slot is None:
+                    request.save_last_block_key = key
+            elif slot is None:
+                request.save_last_block_key = None
+            else:
+                request.save_block_keys[slot] = None
+        worker._layerwise_session_tracker.register_put_keys(
+            request.req_id,
+            ((key, block_index) for key, _, block_index in key_slots if key in started),
+        )
+
+    def _prepare_single_get_session(self, request: ReqMeta) -> list[tuple[str, int, int | None]]:
+        worker = self._worker
+        request.load_block_keys = []
+        request.load_last_block_key = None
+        request.load_keys = []
+        current_entries: list[tuple[str, int]] = []
+        load_spec = request.load_spec
+        if load_spec is not None and load_spec.can_load:
+            cached_tokens = load_spec.kvpool_cached_tokens
+            if not worker.use_eagle:
+                cached_tokens = load_spec.pool_hit_tokens
+            start_block = load_spec.vllm_cached_tokens // worker.block_size
+            cached_full_blocks = cached_tokens // worker.block_size
+            group_block_hashes = get_block_hashes(request.block_hashes, worker.block_size, worker.hash_block_size)
+            end_block = min(cached_full_blocks, len(group_block_hashes))
+            for block_index in range(start_block, end_block):
+                current_entries.append(
+                    (
+                        worker._make_layerwise_full_key(0, block_hash_to_str(group_block_hashes[block_index])),
+                        block_index,
+                    )
+                )
+            needs_last_block = cached_tokens % worker.block_size != 0 or (
+                cached_tokens > 0 and end_block < cached_full_blocks
+            )
+            partial_block_index = cached_full_blocks if cached_tokens % worker.block_size else cached_full_blocks - 1
+            if needs_last_block and 0 <= partial_block_index < len(request.block_ids):
+                current_entries.append(
+                    (
+                        worker._make_layerwise_full_key(0, f"{request.req_id}_lastblock"),
+                        partial_block_index,
+                    )
+                )
+
+        load_entries = worker._layerwise_session_tracker.prepare_load_entries(request.req_id, current_entries)
+        valid_entries = [
+            (key, block_index) for key, block_index in load_entries if 0 <= block_index < len(request.block_ids)
+        ]
+        if not valid_entries:
+            return []
+        request.load_key_block_offset = 0
+        request.load_block_keys = [None] * (max(block_index for _, block_index in valid_entries) + 1)
+        key_slots: list[tuple[str, int, int | None]] = []
+        for key, block_index in valid_entries:
+            request.load_block_keys[block_index] = key
+            key_slots.append((key, request.block_ids[block_index], block_index))
+        return key_slots
+
+    # --- hybrid (multi-group) protocol ---------------------------------------------
+
+    def _prepare_hybrid_sessions(self, requests: list[ReqMeta]) -> dict[int, list[ReqMeta]]:
+        worker = self._worker
+        worker._layer_load_aborted.clear()
+        with worker._put_started_keys_lock:
+            previously_started = worker._put_started_keys.copy()
+        try:
+            return self._prepare_group_sessions(requests)
+        except Exception:
+            # Preparation has not submitted payload transfers yet. Roll back other
+            # groups too if a later group's session allocation fails.
+            worker._layer_load_aborted.set()
+            with worker._put_started_keys_lock:
+                keys = list(worker._put_started_keys - previously_started)
+            worker._queue_layerwise_revoke_keys(keys)
+            self.finish_sessions()
+            raise
+
+    def _prepare_group_sessions(self, requests: list[ReqMeta]) -> dict[int, list[ReqMeta]]:
+        """Views isolate per-group key slots while preserving real request ownership.
+
+        Hybrid pooling publishes only complete blocks. Partial compressor/SWA state
+        is not a portable snapshot: the shared coordinator supplies aligned extents
+        and masks for the reachable state at each boundary.
+        """
+        worker = self._worker
+        result: dict[int, list[ReqMeta]] = {group: [] for group in range(worker.num_kv_cache_groups)}
+        get_slots: list[tuple[ReqMeta, str, int, int | None]] = []
+        tracker = worker._layerwise_session_tracker
+        worker._current_layerwise_request_ids = {request.req_id for request in requests}
+        worker._current_layerwise_last_chunk_req_ids = {request.req_id for request in requests if request.is_last_chunk}
+        for request in requests:
+            cached_tokens = request.save_start_token
+            if request.load_spec is not None and request.load_spec.can_load:
+                cached_tokens = request.load_spec.kvpool_cached_tokens
+                if not worker.use_eagle and len(worker.cacheable_group_ids) == worker.num_kv_cache_groups:
+                    cached_tokens = request.load_spec.pool_hit_tokens
+            load_masks = worker._compute_reachable_load_masks(request, cached_tokens)
+            for group in worker.cacheable_group_ids:
+                # Skip private rings before deriving token hashes: their physical
+                # capacity need not even be divisible by the hash block size.
+                block_size = worker.grouped_block_size[group]
+                view = copy(request)
+                # Keep the complete group block table: LayerBatchBuilder indexes it
+                # using task.group_id. Only key/session metadata is group-local.
+                view.save_block_keys = []
+                view.load_block_keys = []
+                view.load_keys = []
+                view.save_last_block_key = view.load_last_block_key = None
+                view.partial_block_index = None
+                result[group].append(view)
+                ids = request.block_ids_by_group[group]
+                hashes = get_block_hashes(request.block_hashes, block_size, worker.hash_block_size)
+                load_mask = load_masks[group] if load_masks is not None else None
+                store_mask = request.store_masks[group] if request.store_masks is not None else None
+
+                def key(index, group=group, hashes=hashes):
+                    return worker._make_layerwise_full_key(group, block_hash_to_str(hashes[index]))
+
+                start = request.load_spec.vllm_cached_tokens // block_size if request.load_spec is not None else 0
+                entries = (
+                    [
+                        (key(index), index)
+                        for index in range(start, min(cached_tokens // block_size, len(hashes), len(ids)))
+                        if selected(load_mask, index)
+                    ]
+                    if request.load_spec is not None and request.load_spec.can_load
+                    else []
+                )
+                entries = tracker.prepare_load_entries(request.req_id, entries, group_id=group)
+                entries = [
+                    (name, index)
+                    for name, index in entries
+                    if start <= index < min(len(ids), cached_tokens // block_size) and selected(load_mask, index)
+                ]
+                view.load_key_block_offset = 0
+                view.load_block_keys = [None] * (max((index for _, index in entries), default=-1) + 1)
+                for name, index in entries:
+                    view.load_block_keys[index] = name
+                    get_slots.append((view, name, ids[index], index))
+
+                start = request.save_start_token // block_size
+                end = min(request.save_end_token // block_size, len(hashes), len(ids))
+                if request.load_spec is not None:
+                    start = request.load_spec.clamp_save_start(start, block_size)
+                view.save_end_token = end * block_size
+                view.save_key_block_offset = start
+                view.save_block_keys = [None] * max(0, end - start)
+                if not request.can_save or not worker._is_layerwise_save_owner(group):
+                    continue
+                key_indices = [(key(index), index) for index in range(start, end) if selected(store_mask, index)]
+                names = [name for name, _ in key_indices]
+                with worker._put_started_keys_lock:
+                    started = set(names) & worker._put_started_keys
+                new = [name for name in names if name not in started]
+                # A block that is already readable in the pool must never be re-put.
+                # Mooncake refuses to write into a committed object
+                # (MMC_UNMATCHED_KEY) and the aborted session leaves that object
+                # unusable for every reader. `_put_started_keys` only covers writers
+                # still in flight, and it is cleared once a session commits, so
+                # every later request sharing the prefix — and every concurrent
+                # prefill rank, whose keys carry no DP component — would otherwise
+                # re-open a session over the same committed blocks forever.
+                # The non-layerwise path filters through
+                # Backend.requires_exists_before_put; the hybrid path must too.
+                if new:
+                    missing = worker._filter_pool_existing_keys(new)
+                    if len(missing) != len(new):
+                        logger.debug(
+                            "Mooncake hybrid: req=%s group=%d skipping %d/%d blocks already pooled",
+                            request.req_id,
+                            group,
+                            len(new) - len(missing),
+                            len(new),

+                    new = missing
+                if new:
+                    try:
+                        codes = worker._start_layerwise_put_keys(new, sum(worker.group_block_len[group]))

+                        # owns nothing to revoke — and revoking a key another rank
+                        # committed would discard its object. Report instead of
+                        # acting: this used to be dropped in silence, which is how a
+                        # permanently unhittable pool went unnoticed.
+                        logger.warning(
+                            "Mooncake hybrid put_start rejected %d/%d keys for group %d (codes=%s); "
+                            "those blocks stay unsaved this step.",
+                            len(rejected),
+                            len(new),
+                            group,
+                            [code for code in codes if code != 0][:4],
+                        )
+                    started.update(started_now)
+                    if started_now:
+                        with worker._put_started_keys_lock:
+                            worker._put_started_keys.update(started_now)
+                for name, index in key_indices:
+                    if name in started:
+                        view.save_block_keys[index - start] = name
+                tracker.register_put_keys(
+                    request.req_id, ((name, index) for name, index in key_indices if name in started), group_id=group
+                )
+        worker._open_layerwise_get_sessions(get_slots)
+        return result

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+
+"""GVA plane: the pool stores data behind worker-allocated virtual addresses."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import time
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
+
+import numpy as np
+from vllm.logger import logger
+
+from vllm_ascend.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_pool.ascend_store.layerwise.metadata import (
+    get_partial_block_index,
+)
+from vllm_ascend.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_pool.ascend_store.layerwise.planes.base import (
+    LayerwiseDataPlane,
+)
+from vllm_ascend.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_pool.ascend_store.metadata import (
+    ReqMeta,
+    block_hash_to_str,
+    get_block_hashes,
+)
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from vllm_ascend.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_pool.ascend_store.layerwise.pool_worker import (
+        LayerwiseKVPoolWorker,
+    )
+
+# Read lease TTL (ms) for the layerwise load path. batch_add_lease acquires a
+# read lease before batch_copy(G2L); the lease must cover the asynchronous
+# multi-layer load time.
+LAYERWISE_READ_LEASE_TTL_MS = 5 * 60 * 1000
+MEMCACHE_SSD_HIT_GVA = (1 << 64) - 1
+
+# A partial snapshot can be visible to readers before the rank responsible for
+# saving it has published its final layer.
+MEMCACHE_UNMATCHED_STATE = -3101
+PARTIAL_LEASE_RETRY_COUNT = 10
+PARTIAL_LEASE_RETRY_INTERVAL_S = 0.001
+
+
+class GvaDataPlane(LayerwiseDataPlane):
+    """GVA-addressed pooling: allocate write targets and lease readable GVAs.
+
+    The save path allocates per-group GVAs plus the request-scoped trailing
+    partial block; the load path resolves resident GVAs, rewarm-queries
+    SSD-only keys, and acquires read leases before ``batch_copy(G2L)``.
+    Shared machinery (store handle, key construction, the save-disable
+    circuit breaker, failure recording) stays on the worker and is reached
+    through ``self._worker``.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, worker: LayerwiseKVPoolWorker):
+        self._worker = worker
+
+    def prepare_sessions(self, requests: list[ReqMeta]) -> dict[int, list[ReqMeta]]:
+        """GVA opens no pool sessions; resolve the transfer targets instead.
+
+        Protect the previous partial before allocating the next snapshot:
+        load preparation queries the pool-registered GVA of the previous
+        step's snapshot, so it must complete before save allocation
+        repoints the partial key at a fresh one.
+        """
+        self._prepare_load_gvas(requests)
+        self._alloc_gvas_for_save(requests)
+        return {}
+
+    def finish_sessions(self) -> None:
+        """GVA loads read through worker-held addresses, not pool sessions."""
+
+    # --- save path -----------------------------------------------------------
+
+    def _alloc_gvas_for_save(self, requests: list[ReqMeta]) -> None:
+        worker = self._worker
+        if not worker.use_layerwise_transfer:
+            return
+        if worker.kv_role == "kv_consumer" and not worker.consumer_is_to_put:
+            return
+        for request in requests:
+            if worker._save_disabled.is_set():
+                break
+            if not request.can_save:
+                continue
+            if self._alloc_gvas_for_save_for_request([request]) is False:
+                logger.error("Memcache save preparation failed for %s", request.req_id)
+                worker._save_disabled.set()
+        if worker._save_disabled.is_set():
+            # batch_alloc may return a shared allocation. Stop this step's
+            # saves without deleting keys that another writer may have published.
+            for request in requests:
+                if worker.layerwise_offload and request.can_save:
+                    worker._record_failed_request(request)
+                request.can_save = False
+                request.save_keys = []
+
+    def _alloc_gvas_for_save_for_request(self, requests: list[ReqMeta]) -> bool | None:
+        """Allocate per-group GVA on the worker side right before batch_copy.
+
+        For multi-group models, iterates all KV cache groups and allocates
+        per-group GVAs. Key format: model@group_id@hash@head_or_tp_rank
+        (multi-group) or model@hash@head_or_tp_rank (single-group, backward
+        compat with PR #11585).
+
+        batch_alloc is idempotent, so every write target is allocated fresh
+        within the step and no cross-step GVA cache is kept. Blocks already
+        committed in the pool are filtered out with a medium-agnostic
+        exists check to avoid re-transferring them.
+        """
+        worker = self._worker
+        if not worker.use_layerwise_transfer:
+            return None
+        if not worker.can_put:
+            return None
+        for request in requests:
+            if request.can_save is None or not request.can_save:
+                continue
+            block_hashes = request.block_hashes

+        """External pool coverage in tokens.
+
+        Prefers the raw store-skip hit when the store reported one, else the
+        cached hit length. Load-range planning and save-range clamping share
+        this resolution; policies that must ignore the raw hit (eagle drafts,
+        hybrid groups that are not all cacheable) keep guards at call sites.

+        return self.kvpool_store_skip_tokens if self.kvpool_store_skip_tokens is not None else self.kvpool_cached_tokens
+
+    def clamp_save_start(self, start_block: int, block_size: int) -> int:
+        """Clamp ``start_block`` up past blocks the pool hit already covers.
+
+        No-op unless the hit is loadable (``can_load``): an unloadable hit
+        never trims the save range.

[Community] nominate AuroraEmiya as committer (#22289)

- ✅ **Review Quality:**
He has reviewed [113
PRs](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pulls?q=is%3Apr+reviewed-by%3AAuroraEmiya+-author%3AAuroraEmiya),
with a strong focus on Triton operators. His reviews help maintain
consistent standards for operator correctness, performance, testing, and
documentation, demonstrating a deep understanding of Triton development
on Ascend. Representative reviews include
[#16350](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/16350#discussion_r4089273333)
and
[#15212](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/15212#discussion_r3893208918).
 
- ✅ **Sustained Contributions:**
Since May 2026, he has contributed [38 merged
PRs](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Amerged+author%3AAuroraEmiya),
including release backports, with sustained contributions to Triton
operator adaptation and optimization, MRV2 correctness, and
native-operator build infrastructure. His merged performance
improvements cover at least six distinct Triton operators.
 
- ✅ **Quality Contributions:**
**Triton Operator Adaptation and Optimization:**
He adapted the fused Top-K/Top-P kernel to Ascend and fixed numerical
and boundary-handling issues
([#13847](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/13847)). He
optimized rejection resampling
([#15573](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/15573)) and
categorical sampling
([#16269](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/16269))
through Vector Core-aware scheduling and hierarchical sampling,
achieving 4.59× resampling-kernel speedup and 553×–1,381×
categorical-sampling speedup over the previous NPU Gumbel-Max
implementation in measured kernel benchmarks, while preserving sampling
distributions.
He also optimized grammar-bitmask processing
([#14525](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/14525)),
DFlash input preparation
([#15314](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/15314)),
penalty bincount
([#20258](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/20258)), and
fused MiniMax-M3 QK norm/RoPE/cache preparation
([#20308](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/20308)).
**Operator Maintainability and Development Standards:**
He separated legacy V1 Triton operators and consolidated V2 operator
paths, updating production callers, warmup registrations, tests, and
documentation
([#20027](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/20027)). He
also reduced unnecessary resampling JIT specialization
([#17575](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/17575)) and
maintained numerical and statistical tests alongside operator changes.
**Native-Operator Build Cache and CI:**
He designed and implemented the persistent, fine-grained csrc L1 build
cache, including per-action validation, concurrency protection, and CI
integration
([#16718](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/16718)). He
continued improving its reliability and usability through cross-runner
transport fixes
([#18123](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/18123)),
per-operator cache-version management
([#18793](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/18793)), and
compatible cache reuse across source checkouts
([#20905](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/20905)).
**Some Important Bugfixes:**
He fixed biased residual-token sampling in speculative decoding
([#18657](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/18657)),
restored N-gram speculative-decoding compatibility with Triton 3.6.0
([#19912](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/19912)), and
resolved concurrent publication-directory creation failures in
native-operator builds
([#18923](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/18923)).
 
- ✅ **Community Involvement:**
He has participated in [7 issue
discussions](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/issues?q=is%3Aissue+commenter%3AAuroraEmiya),
helping users investigate Triton compatibility and native-operator build
failures. Representative contributions include following up on an
upstream Triton-Ascend alignment fix
([#18345](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/issues/18345#issuecomment-6159149877)),
providing build-failure diagnostics
([#21273](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/issues/21273#issuecomment-6764654423)),
and documenting clean-rebuild requirements after CANN version changes
([#18215](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/18215)).

[Feature] Enable PCP for Kimi RecoverSSM (#21941)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Enable experimental prefill context parallelism (PCP) for Kimi K3 and
K3.1 with RecoverSSM by providing the permutation and mask metadata
required by the KDA path.

Share the PCP capture-configuration and buffer initialization between
the ordinary Kimi KDA and RecoverSSM builders, preserving their
respective base-class initialization. Reuse the existing Kimi KDA PCP
metadata attachment logic.

Update the Kimi K3/K3.1 release fragments in response to #21549 review:
clarify the limited validation scope and remove unqualified A3/A5
hardware-matrix tags pending broader validation.

### Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?

Yes. Kimi K3 and K3.1 can use RecoverSSM with prefill context
parallelism (PCP).

### How was this patch tested?

- Documentation follow-ups `d5d26bbb3` and `8344bf4cf`: targeted
markdownlint, codespell and typos checks passed; the release-note YAML
fragments present at the time parsed and `git diff --check` passed.
`bash format.sh ci` was attempted but interrupted while installing the
actionlint environment on Windows. No NPU test was performed for these
documentation-only commits.

- Follow-up commit `9e8ef5901`: CPU unit tests in an isolated Ascend
image, with NPU hardware mocked: `python3 -m pytest -q
tests/ut/models/test_kimi_recoverssm_metadata.py
tests/ut/models/test_glm5next_recoverssm_metadata.py
tests/ut/ops/test_kimi_kda_pcp_context.py
tests/ut/ops/test_kimi_kda_pcp.py` — 80 passed. The image's vLLM
checkout was `4ba787ec9959e566d3b587a796dff07673324da5`, not the vLLM
main revision listed below.
- The new tests execute the real RecoverSSM builder initialization,
parent `build`, and `build_for_cudagraph_capture` metadata path. They
cover speculative-decode metadata, PCP dummy indices, a global batch
larger than the local capture limit, and stable buffer addresses when
metadata is refreshed. The PCP group and model-layer RecoverSSM context
are test substitutes; this is not an NPU graph replay test. In an
isolated negative-control copy with PCP attachment removed, both new
cases failed with missing `pcp_restore_idx`.
- Ruff check and format passed. The repository-wide `format.sh ci` check
could not complete successfully on Windows: actionlint installation
stalled, typos encountered a path/config error, and several hooks
required unavailable `/bin/bash`, shellcheck, or Python executables. CI
must run the full check.
- `python3 -m pytest -q test_kimi_recoverssm_metadata.py`: 4 passed,
including new coverage for PCP=1/2 buffer sizing, config isolation,
token permutations and padding masks. The test file was run in the
Ascend container against the patched source.
- Four Ascend 950DT nodes, PP4/TP1/PCP8, RecoverSSM enabled, prefix
caching disabled: a real 16,384-input-token, one-output-token request
completed successfully.
- An earlier full-expert performance run was cancelled on request. The
subsequent experts8 performance run below completed. It does not
validate accuracy or multi-token speculative-decode recovery.

**Four-node pure-prefill performance, Kimi K3.1 experts8**

- Code: vLLM Ascend PR head `9e8ef5901fe564ba9310aefc9272b10bad7942de`;
vLLM core `4ba787ec9959e566d3b587a796dff07673324da5` (not the vLLM main
revision listed below). Four Ascend 950DT nodes (32 NPUs), PP4/TP1/PCP8,
RecoverSSM enabled, DSpark3, eager execution.
- AISBench GSM8K: 16,384 input tokens and 1 output token; concurrency
144, 2,016 total requests, one warmup request, prefix caching disabled.
No profiling was collected. All 2,016 requests succeeded, and all
request details reported the requested input and output lengths.
- The following original AISBench tables cover its **stable** interval:
1,872 requests, not the full 2,016. Average client concurrency was
143.8168, maximum 144; aggregate input throughput was 31,963.5653
token/s and mean TTFT was 73,718.0 ms.
- In 973 service-metric samples with at least 100 running plus waiting
requests, the mean was 4.00 running and 137.45 waiting. This sampling
interval is not identical to the AISBench stable interval; client
in-flight concurrency is not the number of requests executing on the
service.
- Output length 1 is a prefill-focused test. ITL and multi-token

commits.message:
[Refactor][Observability] Merged due bus for dump + CPU/Gloo only (#21375)

## Summary
- Reuse the last-PP TP **merged due bus** for dump delivery even when
hot-reload is off (`config_due` stays false); replace TP dump claim with
local stash for `tp<=1`; delete dead `sync_due_bits` / `sync_task_bus`.
- Pin remaining due-bit collective to **cpu_group / Gloo only** (no
HCCL/`device_group` fallback); keep `wave_idx`.
- Rename misleading entrypoints to match behavior: `wave_head_sync` /
`begin_wave` / `end_of_wave`, `broadcast_due_bits_from_src`,
`persist_bootstrap_config`,
`manual_dump_armed`/`remaining`/`consume_manual_dump`,
`is_action_leader`. JSON keys unchanged.

Supersedes #21363 and #20695.

## Test plan
- [x] `tests/ut/runtime_config/test_dist.py` /
`test_runtime_config_core.py`
- [x] runtime_guard hooks / hot-path / bus_worker / action / manual_dump
/ review regressions
- [x] CI gate on this PR

- vLLM main:
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/ba15685ab7f4f5fbed8630bbb7441f8837e76fbe

---------

Signed-off-by: djh95 <dengjiahui95@gmail.com>
Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

[Community] nominate zhangxinyuehfad as committer (#22279)

He is nominated primarily for his professional expertise in CI/CD
infrastructure and release engineering, his key contributions to the
accuracy evaluation and reporting system, nightly and weekly regression
pipelines, multi-hardware delivery (container images and wheels),
trigger-based gating, and cluster scheduling, as well as his sustained
substantial improvements around these areas.
Since March 2025, @zhangxinyuehfad has contributed around 323 pull
requests (257 merged), delivering nearly 30,000 lines of changes across
roughly 1,270 files, covering 15 releases from v0.8.4 to v0.32.0. Beyond
the pipelines themselves, he built the accuracy and nightly regression
infrastructure that gates every release, and the AI-assisted
documentation translation pipeline that was later handed over to another
contributor for ongoing maintenance.
I believe his participation will further strengthen CI/CD reliability,
multi-hardware delivery and upstream alignment on vLLM Ascend.

✅ Review Quality

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pulls?q=commenter%3Azhangxinyuehfad
He has commented on 420 pull requests and submitted formal reviews on
228, including 121 approvals and 80 review comments, raising 92
file-level review threads across 55 pull requests. His review focus is
CI/CD workflows, test coverage and infrastructure changes.

✅ Quality Contributions
- Accuracy Evaluation & Reporting: He is the primary contributor of the
model accuracy verification system, having designed and delivered it
from manual benchmarking to automated CI regression with dashboard-based
reporting:
- [CI Add model basic accuracy test (Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct)
#460](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/460)
- [CI Add accuracy ci for DP and EP and TP and ETP
#1140](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/1140)
- [CI Support artifact collection and dashboard reporting for nightly
tests #7102](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/7102)
- Nightly Regression Pipelines: He built the scheduled regression
pipelines covering 310P, A2 and A3 hardware, including the A3 560T
super-node cluster:
- [CI Add e2e test for 310p
#1879](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/1879)
- [CI add nightly test workflow and config for A3 560T clusters
#12270](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/12270)
- Multi-Hardware Delivery: He established the build and distribution
system for container images and wheels across 310P, A2, A3 and A5,
parameterized so that supporting new hardware only extends a matrix
instead of adding a pipeline:
- [CI Add multi-hardware wheel build and release workflow
#7312](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/7312)
- [CI Chain nightly base image and nightly image builds
#18988](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/18988)
- [CI Add commit-pinned image build mode for vllm + vllm-ascend
#10538](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/10538)
- Trigger-Based Gating: He delivered the contributor-facing entry points
that let a PR request targeted test runs, and decoupled test definitions
from workflow files:
- [CI support nightly ci for per pr by labels
#6483](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/6483)
- [CI externalize test config and add /nightly dispatch resolver
#10614](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/10614)
- Cluster Scheduling: He optimized NPU cluster utilization for nightly
workloads, cutting the A3 nightly makespan from 11h25m to 5h05m and
moving from taint-based isolation to priority-based scheduling:
- [CI Optimize nightly A3 test scheduling
#11500](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/11500)
- [CI Refactor nightly scheduling and drain PR runs before the nightly
window #21158](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/21158)
- Documentation Automation: He built the AI-assisted translation
pipeline that keeps the Chinese documentation in sync with the English
source through Sphinx PO files, and stabilized it against PO corruption
before handing it over to another contributor:
- [CI Add AI auto translate Docs
#6682](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/6682)
- [CI Fix auto-translation PO file corruption and improve PR title
#8135](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/8135)
- Upstream Alignment: He turned vLLM ref selection from manual switching
into a branch-driven rule within the sustained main2main work:
- [CI Select vLLM ref by PR base branch for E2E and CPU UT
#19902](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/19902)

[CI] Align fla_npu pins on 26.10.0+feature and classify its GDN window (#21203)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

#22141 bumped `FLA_VERSION` to `26.10.0+feature` in the six Dockerfiles
but left the four workflow pins and the GDN window registry on `26.9.1`,
so every CPU unit-test run on top of main fails in the guard added by
#21936:

```
FAILED tests/ut/ops/test_gdn_window_guard.py::test_declared_pins_agree fla_npu pins disagree: ['26.10.0+feature', '26.9.1']
FAILED tests/ut/ops/test_gdn_window_guard.py::test_declared_window_is_known conflicting fla_npu pins: Dockerfile*=26.10.0+feature,
  .github/workflows/*=26.9.1
```

The second failure is the same root cause: `_declared_window()` returns
the `UNKNOWN` sentinel when the pins disagree, hence the `assert <object
object at ...> is not <object object at ...>` line.

This PR completes the bump:

- Workflows now install
`flash-linear-attention-npu-*===26.10.0+feature`:
`_selected_tests.yaml`, `_selected_tests_upstream.yaml`,
`schedule_e2e_upstream_test.yaml`, `schedule_main2main.yaml`. CI
therefore
  exercises the same wheel the images ship, instead of 26.9.1.
- `KNOWN_OPP_WINDOWS` gains `"26.10.0+feature": 8`.
- `dependency_version_management.md` follows the new pin, and the
main2main example is corrected to the mirror pin the workflow actually
uses (the old dev-wheel download snippet no longer matched any file).

The v26.10.0-feature wheel still contains the fixed-window AscendC
kernel, so no dispatch change is needed: `recurrent_gated_delta_rule`
has no `arch22`/`arch35` OPP directory and its header declares `MAX_MTP
= 8` (verified in the published a2 wheel). The `8`-token cap, the
`spec_state_indices_tensor.shape[1] > _MAX_RECURRENT_GDN_TOKENS` gate,
and the A2 `gdn_fixed_spec_recurrent_fallback_min_query_len=9`
workaround all stay.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

### How was this patch tested?

---

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [ ] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: I reviewed whether this change
involves
boundary conditions (e.g. empty input, single/zero element, min/max
values,
off-by-one, sequence-length limits, integer overflow). Where applicable,
I
added unit tests covering these edge cases in `tests/ut/` or
`tests/e2e/`.
- [ ] **Regression test**: If this PR fixes a bug, I added a regression
test
  that would fail without the fix.
- [ ] **Error / failure path coverage**: I covered abnormal paths
(exceptions,
timeouts, out-of-range, division by zero) in addition to the happy path.
- [ ] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: New tests assert real behavior
and are
  not written merely to satisfy CI.
- [ ] **Performance impact**: If this PR touches a performance-sensitive
path,
  I attached benchmark results and added performance regression tests.

[Community] nominate winson-00178005 as committer (#22272)

- ✅Review Quality:
31 PR reviewed and 48 PR commented in the main repository:[
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pulls?q=is%3Apr+reviewed-by%3Awinson-00178005](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pulls?q=is%3Apr+reviewed-by%3Awinson-00178005)
Three of them are worth calling out. Each is a silent correctness risk
rather than a style comment:
1. PR #10802, PD disaggregation. pd_tp_ratio is computed as
prefill_tp_size // decode_tp_size, which yields 0 when prefill_tp_size <
decode_tp_size (2 // 4 = 0); the ratio is then silently wrong instead of
failing fast, and the HND KV transfer path skips MLA/sparse without a
design note. Both were fixed before merge:[
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/10802](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/10802)
2. PR #10842, AscendSFA. Assigning the shared o_proj_full_pool after
all_gather_async lets the main model and the MTP draft model overwrite
each other, a dtype mismatch that produces wrong output rather than a
crash. He pushed for instance-level isolation:[
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/10842](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/10842)
3. PR #10859, W8A8 dynamic quantization. The code reads an attribute
misspelled as inderxer_wq_b (correct: indexer_wq_b), so getattr always
returns None and the indexer W8A8 path is silently disabled, an accuracy
regression no test would catch. The typo was corrected and the
quant_matmul fallback without pertoken_scale was confirmed:[
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/10859](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/10859)
- ✅ Sustained and Major Contributions
His scope in the community is engineering capability: CI/CD, developer
testing and quality dashboards.
138 merged PRs across the vllm-ascend org as of 2026-11-12, of which 102
are in vllm_ascend_dashboard, 3 in vllm-project/vllm-ascend and 1 in
vllm-ascend-recipes. In the main repository he keeps the test partition
algorithm and the CI pipeline itself (#7588, #14230, #14270):[
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pulls?q=is%3Apr+author%3Awinson-00178005+is%3Amerged](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pulls?q=is%3Apr+author%3Awinson-00178005+is%3Amerged)
Review coverage spans five release cycles, from upstream adaptation to
Ascend 950 and 4-bit quantization:
v0.11.0: #10807, #10824, #10858
v0.13.0: #10862, #10769
v0.18.0: #10781, #10855, #6517
v0.23.0: #10763, #10775, #6733, #10755
v0.30.0: #10806, #10846
- ✅ Quality Contribution:
1. Feature Owner, vllm_ascend_dashboard (2026.03). The community CI /
model / performance dashboard is a full-stack service (FastAPI + React,
MySQL migration, Docker Compose) that the community uses daily to read
CI status, model validation and performance metrics. He contributed 166
commits and 106 PRs (102 merged), covering the PR pipeline data model,
contributor ranking and the AI evaluation view, and he acts as release
manager of its releases:[
https://github.com/vllm-ascend/vllm_ascend_dashboard](https://github.com/vllm-ascend/vllm_ascend_dashboard)
2. Contributor, vllm-ascend-recipes (2026.07). The deployment Recipes
site (Astro, 16 model recipes, EN/ZH, cascade wizard and /models.json
API) turns model x NPU x precision validation into copy-pasteable
deployment guides for Atlas 800 A2/A3. His part is model data, CI
(validate / typecheck / lint) and PR Netlify preview:[
https://github.com/vllm-ascend/vllm-ascend-recipes](https://github.com/vllm-ascend/vllm-ascend-recipes)
- ✅Community Involvement:
1. Issues. He filed the daily regression pipeline for broken-window
detection (#13953, #14028), the PR coverage gate (#14119) and a CPU-only
build check (#11928):[
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/issues?q=is%3Aissue+author%3Awinson-00178005](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/issues?q=is%3Aissue+author%3Awinson-00178005)
2. Sharing. CI/CD progress and nightly governance on the community
weekly meeting and the TMG meeting, plus the Recipes wizard design and
dashboard operation.
3. Docs and onboarding. He maintains the bilingual Recipes documentation
(EN/ZH, 16 recipes) and the community pipeline caretaking mechanism.

commits.message:
[Community] nominate lcfenglinwan as committer (#22269)

I would like to nominate @lcfenglinwan as a vLLM Ascend maintainer for
the quantization and DeepSeek sparse attention / MoE domains. He has
been a sustained, high-signal contributor since early 2026 and has
become one of the busiest reviewers of the quantization, DSA/SFA
attention and MoE dispatch code.
He started in Aug. 2025 by reporting a real bug
([#2468](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/issues/2468),
DeepSeek DBO under TP), and has landed[ 24 merged
PRs](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Amerged+author%3Alcfenglinwan)
(including 3 release backports) across v0.18.0 → v0.30.0: W4A4/W4A8
MXFP4 and W8A8 MXFP8 quantization for Ascend 950 (A5), MC2/MegaMoE
quantized communication, the FP8/INT8 quantized KV cache path, and the
DeepSeek-V4 sparse-attention operator stack. The KV-cache-dtype design
was also carried upstream-first: the RFC and implementation for
pluggable KV cache data types are merged in vLLM
([vllm#51751](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/51751) /[
vllm#52670](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52670)), and vLLM
Ascend now registers its own dtypes instead of patching vLLM.
 
- ✅ Review Quality:
He has completed[ 80+ reviews on PRs authored by
others](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pulls?q=is%3Apr+commenter%3Alcfenglinwan+-author%3Alcfenglinwan)
since Mar. 2026 (93 review threads in total), concentrated in
quantization, DSA/SFA sparse attention, MoE token dispatch, KV cache
dtype and KV transfer. His reviews catch correctness, memory-lifetime
and architecture-consistency problems rather than style, for example:
-[ [Feature][Model] Use SparseFlashMla for DSV4 A5 BF16
KV](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/13716): pushed back
on redundant dtype branching and asked for a single
uses_explicit_bf16_kv condition.
-[ [BugFix][Platform] Declare the KV cache dtypes DeepSeek V4 can
store](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/18891): rejected
an __mro__-based parent-class check and spotted duplicated validation
between platform.py and the attention layer.
-[ [Refactor][Attention] Move the DSpark draft top-k contract into the
SparseFlashMla
adapters](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/19989):
argued for reverting the helpers and branches added by #19220 so that
the top-k contract lives in one place
 
- ✅ Sustained and Major Contributions
24 merged PRs, of which 21 are original changes and 3 are release
backports (#11853, #12029, #18808), with steady activity in almost every
month since Mar. 2026 — A5 quantization in Apr./Jun., MoE dispatcher and
MegaMoE in Jul./Aug., FP8/INT8 KV cache and DSV4 sparse attention in
Sep./Oct.:[
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Amerged+author%3Alcfenglinwan](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Amerged+author%3Alcfenglinwan)
What makes this sustained rather than a burst of drive-by fixes is that
his work tracks the release train and the hardware bring-up: the same
person delivers the A5 W4A4 MXFP4 kernel integration, the block-size
fixes that unblock DSV4.1, and the documentation that lets users deploy
DSV4-Flash on Ascend 950DT.
He deliberately works upstream-first rather than carrying Ascend-only
patches:[ [RFC]: Pluggable KV Cache Data Types
(vllm#51751)](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/51751) and its
implementation[
vllm#52670](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52670) move the
KV-cache-dtype registry into vLLM core, so any out-of-tree backend —
including vLLM Ascend — can register dtypes such as int8 without monkey
patches. This removes long-term maintenance burden from vLLM Ascend
instead of adding to it.
 
- ✅ Quality Contribution:
**Quantization for Ascend 950: **
-[ [Ascend950][quant][Feature] W4A4 MXFP4 quantization support for
Ascend950](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/7877): the
first W4A4 scheme in vLLM Ascend, with
AscendW4A4MXFP4DynamicLinearMethod /
AscendW4A4MXFP4DynamicFusedMoEMethod and the grouped-matmul-swiglu path.
-[ [Refactor] refactor fp8
config](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/13651):
AscendFp8Config now inherits the upstream Fp8Config and
AscendDeepseekV4FP8Config handles DSV4, followed by the quant-name fix
in[ #14490](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/14490).
**Quantized KV cache: **
-[ [Refactor][Quantization]KV cache quantization dtype specified by the
--kv-cache-dtype
parameter](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/15514): the
KV / SFA C8 / indexer C8 dtypes are now derived from the user-visible
--kv-cache-dtype and --attention-config.indexer_kv_dtype (fp8/int8)
instead of being guessed from the hardware profile, static quantization
becomes explicit with a clear startup error instead of a silent
unquantized fallback, and the C8 sparse layouts are gated on the
actually quantized dtype.
**DeepSeek-V4 sparse attention: **
-[ [Attention][Feature]Integrate mixed_quant_sparse_flash_mla op for the
DeepSeek-V4 FP8 KV
path](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/17354): unifies
the DSV4 sparse-attention path on the cann_ops_transformer
MixedQuantSparseFlashMla family, deletes the in-tree KvCompressEpilog
custom op (kernel, tiling, CMake and bindings), moves the FP8 cache to
the 608 B/token PA_BBND layout, and removes NPU→CPU syncs from the hot
path.
MoE dispatcher and quantized communication:
-[ [Refactor]Refactor token dispatcher routing initialization for
quantized alltoall
MoE](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/13641):
consolidates two permutes into one torch_npu.npu_moe_init_routing_v2
call, 231.6us → 192.1us on DeepSeek-V4 W8A8.
- ✅ Community Involvement:
He is one of the most responsive people in the issue tracker: involved
in[ 100+ PR and issue
threads](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/issues?q=commenter%3Alcfenglinwan+-author%3Alcfenglinwan)
and personally driving 14 user-reported problems, mostly the hard
quantization and attention ones.
In short: deep quantization expertise, ownership of the DeepSeek-V4
quantized KV cache path, upstream-first instincts, and steady
high-signal review. I believe he would be a great addition to the vLLM
Ascend maintainer team.
- vLLM main:
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/ba15685ab7f4f5fbed8630bbb7441f8837e76fbe

Signed-off-by: wangxiyuan <wangxiyuan1007@gmail.com>

[CI] Remove the synchronize trigger now that /run is live (#21939)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR, #21434, is a follow-up action to remove the automatic
synchronization trigger in the E2E CI workflow. Since pushing new
commits no longer automatically triggers the CI gate, developers must
use the /run slash command (or trigger via label changes) to run the
full PR gate on the latest commit. This measure prevents intermediate
commits from unnecessarily occupying resources in the NPU runner pool.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. (Documentation-only updates are not considered user-facing changes).

### How was this patch tested?

Not applicable (documentation changes only).

[Community] nominate zhenwenqi2024 as committer (#22264)

Zhen Wenqi is a candidate for vLLM Ascend Maintainer. Since June 2025,
he has contributed to NPU ModelRunner, context parallelism, and MoE
execution. His work has focused on reusing upstream interfaces for
shared logic and keeping Ascend-specific behavior within the plugin.
- ✅ Review Quality:
As of November 13, 2026, GitHub lists[ 217 PRs he
reviewed](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pulls?q=is%3Apr%20reviewed-by%3Azhenwenqi2024%20-author%3Azhenwenqi2024)
in vLLM Ascend, excluding his own PRs. In[
#20194](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/20194#discussion_r4521843128),
he traced the C2 fallback and identified a RoPE gather that could never
run. The author removed it. In[
#21040](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/21040#discussion_r4509027231),
he suggested calling the upstream GDN checkpoint builder directly while
preserving prefill row alignment. The change was adopted and merged. In[
#21417](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/21417#discussion_r4522442882),
he proposed reusing the upstream padding mask. The author identified a
stale-mask risk in ModelRunner V2 and fixed per-batch refresh in[
#21475](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/21475). The
current #21417 patch uses ForwardContext.is_padding.
- ✅ Sustained Contributions:
GitHub records[ 37 merged vLLM Ascend
PRs](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pulls?q=is%3Apr%20is%3Amerged%20author%3Azhenwenqi2024)
and[ 3 merged upstream vLLM
PRs](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pulls?q=is%3Apr%20is%3Amerged%20author%3Azhenwenqi2024)
as of November 13, 2026. His work includes vectorizing SFA
sequence-length computation
([#11762](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/11762)),
fixing dummy-slot invalidation before attention metadata is built
([#15362](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/15362)), and
backporting the shared-expert multistream changes
([#18122](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/18122)).
- ✅ Quality Contributions:
He proposed the NPU ModelRunner refactor in[
#5449](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/issues/5449) and
implemented two core changes.[
#4764](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/4764) reused the
upstream GPUModelRunner and removed a net 1,139 lines across the changed
files.[ #5214](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/5214)
consolidated PCP/DCP handling in a dedicated manager. He also proposed
the shared-expert multistream redesign
([#15353](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/issues/15353)),
clarified stream dependencies
([#15352](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/15352)), and
staged quantized input preparation and compute
([#17255](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/17255)).
For HiSparse, his merged upstream work covers the device backend
interface ([#62592](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62592)),
bounded prefetch
([#63801](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63801)), and cleanup
of temporary KV bindings after graph profiling
([#64989](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64989)). The Ascend
backend foundation remains in progress
([#20926](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/20926)).
- ✅ Community Involvement:
He has opened[ 12 issues and
RFCs](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20author%3Azhenwenqi2024),
including a proposal on MTP prefix caching
([#20001](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/issues/20001)). In
the DSpark TTFT regression discussion
([#19116](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/issues/19116#issuecomment-6315984411)),
he proposed measuring actual prefill-side arrivals and queueing, then
comparing runs at matched arrival rates to isolate the cause.
 
As a Maintainer, he would prioritize reviews in ModelRunner,
long-context inference, speculative decoding, and HiSparse. He would ask
what requires Ascend-specific code, check whether an upstream extension
point already fits, and scrutinize AI-generated changes for unnecessary
wrappers, redundant checks, and misplaced logic.
