+# Review Guidance for vllm-ascend
+
+vLLM Ascend is a hardware plugin integrating Ascend NPUs into vLLM. Formatting,
+PR title tags, and PR description templates are enforced by CI (`format.sh ci`,
+check gates) and by the coding agents developers already use — do NOT comment
+on them.
+
+Focus your review on issues that automated tooling cannot catch:
+
+## NPU-specific correctness and performance
+- `tensor.item()`, `.cpu()`, `.tolist()`, or data-dependent control flow on
+  device tensors in hot paths: each forces a host-device synchronization and
+  can stall AsyncScheduler. Suggest device-side alternatives
+  (`torch.argmax`, `torch.sum`, keeping values on device, batching).
+- Unnecessary CPU↔NPU transfers or avoidable copies in hot paths.
+- Long-running-process memory concerns: fragmentation, tensors that should be
+  freed, per-step allocations that could be reused.
+
+## Architecture rules (see AGENTS.md at repo root)
+- New environment variables need strong justification; user-facing config
+  belongs in `--additional-config` via a typed sub-config in
+  `vllm_ascend/ascend_config.py` (follow `EplbConfig`/`RlConfig` patterns).
+  Flag scattered/hardcoded env var access instead of `vllm_ascend.envs`.
+- New patches under `vllm_ascend/patch/`: check the patch is minimal, targets
+  the right layer (`platform/` vs `worker/`), and is a candidate for upstream
+  contribution to vLLM.
+- Model runner changes (`vllm_ascend/worker/v2/model_runner.py`): check
+  existing upstream extension points (inheritance, composition) were considered
+  first, and flag device-side hot-path costs.
+- No new module-level mutable globals; constants (`ALL_UPPER_CASE`) are fine.
+- All imports at top of file, except circular imports, lazy worker-process
+  loading, and `if TYPE_CHECKING:` blocks.
+
+## Triton operators
+- JIT specialization / recompilation risks from changing arguments.
+- Warmup: required variants registered in the component's active registry
+  window; runtime calls reuse the same wrapper as warmup.
+- Device-applicability across Ascend 910B / 910C / 310P.
+
+## Docs consistency
+- Behavior changes (config keys, env vars, defaults) should be reflected in the
+  relevant docs (`docs/source/user_guide/configuration/`, additional_config
+  table). Flag docs that contradict the code in the same PR.
+
+## Release notes
+- Every user-facing PR must add `release_notes/fragments/<PR number>.yaml`
+  following `release_notes/TEMPLATE.yaml`.
+- Flag fragments that: describe internal refactors users cannot observe,
+  state performance numbers without a scenario (model/workload/hardware) or an
+  invented magnitude, or change config/env behavior without old→new plus the
+  migration step.
+- Bug-fix fragments should describe the user-visible symptom, not the internal
+  root cause.
+
+## Testing
+- Changes to kernels, model runners, or config parsing should come with or
+  update CPU-runnable unit tests under `tests/ut`.
+- Do not ask authors for NPU/E2E/performance runs when they lack hardware —
+  that evidence comes from CI; just say so.

[Community] nominate drslark as committer (#22242)

He has made sustained contributions to vLLM-Ascend, particularly in
speculative decoding. Beyond feature development, he has actively
participated in code reviews, upstream alignment, and issue discussions.

- ✅ **Review Quality:**

He has submitted more than 500 reviews across more than 180 distinct
vLLM-Ascend PRs. [GitHub review
history](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pulls?q=is%3Apr+reviewed-by%3Adrslark+-author%3Adrslark)

In an SFA review, he traced a token-count mismatch to a change in vLLM's
graph execution contract. FULL graphs require the padded token count,
while eager and PIECEWISE execution require the actual token count. That
distinction clarified how the Ascend attention inputs and metadata
needed to follow upstream. [PR #16768
review](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/16768#discussion_r4053082117)

In reviewing DSpark graph support for Model Runner V1, he found that
synchronization dominated the profiled workload. The expected gain did
not justify changes to V1's graph padding and the resulting maintenance
cost. He recommended declining the V1 adaptation and documented Model
Runner V2 as the path for graph support. [PR #16285
review](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/16285#discussion_r4056849065)
· [Issue
#17018](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/issues/17018)

In the DFlash2 review, he traced a local ForwardContext workaround to
the shared ACLGraphWrapper, which assumed a context was always present.
He proposed and validated the upstream-compatible fallback. In the
follow-up PR, sunny-rain-63 fixed the shared wrapper and removed the
DFlash2-specific override. [PR #19512
review](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/19512#discussion_r4450694198)
· [RFC #20763](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/issues/20763)
· [PR #20777](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/20777)

- ✅ **Sustained Contributions:**

He has 54 merged PRs in vLLM-Ascend and two in upstream vLLM, with
sustained contributions across multiple release cycles since October
2025. The upstream changes fixed a Qwen3-Next MTP accuracy bug in
batched inference and skipped an unnecessary token-ID mapping when draft
and target vocabularies matched. [Merged Ascend
PRs](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Amerged+author%3Adrslark)
· [vLLM #30632](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/30632) · [vLLM
#53458](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53458)

- ✅ **Quality Contributions:**

**Model Runner V2 Speculative Decoding — Architecture and
Implementation:**

He authored the design RFC for adapting speculative decoding to Ascend's
Model Runner V2. The design reuses vLLM's draft execution flow and keeps
NPU-specific buffer handling, attention metadata, and ACL graph capture
and replay in focused extension points. It defines how the Ascend
implementation should preserve upstream semantics across eager,
PIECEWISE, and FULL graph execution. [Design RFC
#18466](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/issues/18466)

He implemented the initial EAGLE3 integration, fixed multi-step drafting
accuracy, and corrected graph-mode capture and replay. The later
metadata refactor moved autoregressive and DSpark speculators onto
shared upstream hooks, giving subsequent adaptations a common interface
to build on. [PR
#7885](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/7885) · [PR
#8033](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/8033) · [PR
#8365](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/8365) · [PR
#17461](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/17461)

  **Model Enablement and Runtime Optimization:**

He brought Qwen3-Next MTP to Ascend and extended it to chunked prefill
and full-graph execution. Later work refactored the DeepSeek V4 DSpark
implementation. [PR
#3918](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/3918) · [PR
#4770](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/4770) · [PR
#5477](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/5477) · [PR
#11431](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/11431)

For GLM KDA RecoverSSM, he implemented Triton operators and integrated
the operators into Model Runner V2 to reconstruct and commit recurrent
state after speculative verification. Follow-up PRs enabled prefix
caching and optimized aligned state commits. [PR
#20128](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/20128) · [PR
#20131](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/20131) · [PR
#20369](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/20369) · [PR
#20474](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/20474)

- ✅ **Community Involvement:**

He followed up on EAGLE3 accuracy with sequence parallelism and
investigated a drop in EAGLE3 acceptance rates with QuaRot. For QuaRot,
he explained how the target's rotated hidden states affected the drafter
and shared a weight-conversion tool that folds the inverse rotation into
the drafter's first projection, avoiding a separate runtime operation.
He also published the Q4 speculative decoding roadmap for community
discussion. [Issue
#5825](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/issues/5825) ·
[QuaRot analysis and
tool](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/issues/5974#issuecomment-3763914824)
· [Roadmap
#18827](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/issues/18827)

Model Runner V2. The design reuses vLLM's draft execution flow and keeps
NPU-specific buffer handling, attention metadata, and ACL graph capture
and replay in focused extension points. It defines how the Ascend
implementation should preserve upstream semantics across eager,
PIECEWISE, and FULL graph execution. [Design RFC
#18466](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/issues/18466)

He implemented the initial EAGLE3 integration, fixed multi-step drafting
accuracy, and corrected graph-mode capture and replay. The later
metadata refactor moved autoregressive and DSpark speculators onto
shared upstream hooks, giving subsequent adaptations a common interface
to build on. [PR
#7885](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/7885) · [PR
#8033](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/8033) · [PR
#8365](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/8365) · [PR
#17461](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/17461)

  **Model Enablement and Runtime Optimization:**

He brought Qwen3-Next MTP to Ascend and extended it to chunked prefill
and full-graph execution. Later work refactored the DeepSeek V4 DSpark
implementation. [PR
#3918](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/3918) · [PR
#4770](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/4770) · [PR
#5477](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/5477) · [PR
#11431](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/11431)

For GLM KDA RecoverSSM, he implemented Triton operators and integrated
the operators into Model Runner V2 to reconstruct and commit recurrent
state after speculative verification. Follow-up PRs enabled prefix
caching and optimized aligned state commits. [PR
#20128](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/20128) · [PR
#20131](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/20131) · [PR
#20369](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/20369) · [PR
#20474](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/20474)

- ✅ **Community Involvement:**

He followed up on EAGLE3 accuracy with sequence parallelism and
investigated a drop in EAGLE3 acceptance rates with QuaRot. For QuaRot,
he explained how the target's rotated hidden states affected the drafter
and shared a weight-conversion tool that folds the inverse rotation into
the drafter's first projection, avoiding a separate runtime operation.
He also published the Q4 speculative decoding roadmap for community
discussion. [Issue
#5825](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/issues/5825) ·
[QuaRot analysis and
tool](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/issues/5974#issuecomment-3763914824)

[Ops][Feature] Enable adaptive verification with LM head TP (#21585)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR enables adaptive verification with LM head Tensor Parallelism
(TP) by removing the obsolete LM-head TP gate for adaptive verification.
The current draft-logits alignment trims LM-head padding before the
adaptive estimator reads logits, making the combination safe at
construction.

Additionally, this PR:
- Updates the fine-grained TP support documentation to reflect DSpark
adaptive-verification compatibility and its
confidence-head/full-decode-graph requirements.
- Adds regression test coverage for DSpark LM-head TP construction
validation and model-level draft-logit padding/trimming with adaptive
verification enabled.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. LM-head TP can now be combined with `enable_adaptive_verification`.

### How was this patch tested?

- Syntax compilation passed locally.
- PR CI runs the updated unit tests. The DSpark unit test covers the
construction gate and model-level pad/trim behavior; it does not execute
the confidence head or adaptive budget allocator.
- Accuracy was validated on Ascend NPU in the DSpark scenario with
DeepSeek-V4-Flash across seven validation configurations covering
LM-head TP and adaptive verification, plus the pre-change startup error
check.

[CI][Misc] Update FLA_VERSION to 26.10.0+feature in Dockerfiles (#22141)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR updates the `flash-linear-attention-npu` package used by the A2,
A3 and
A5 images from `26.9.1` to `26.10.0+feature`:

- `Dockerfile` / `Dockerfile.openEuler` (A2)
- `Dockerfile.a3` / `Dockerfile.a3.openEuler` (A3)
- `Dockerfile.a5` / `Dockerfile.a5.openEuler` (A5)

The version comes from the `v26.10.0-feature` release of

[flashserve/flash-linear-attention-npu](https://github.com/flashserve/flash-linear-attention-npu/releases/tag/v26.10.0-feature).
Note that the release tag contains `-feature`, while the wheel version
is
`26.10.0+feature`; the Dockerfiles use the wheel version.

This release contains the KDA forward update that raises the per-pack
sub-sequence limit from 1024 after the underlying `aclIntArray` limit
was
lifted.

No Dockerfile architecture branching is added. The wheels are published
on the
Ascend mirror for both host architectures, and `pip` selects the
matching one:

| Package | x86_64 | aarch64 |
|---|---|---|
| `flash-linear-attention-npu-a2` | yes | yes |
| `flash-linear-attention-npu-a3` | yes | yes |
| `flash-linear-attention-npu-a5` | yes | yes |

The wheel requires glibc >= 2.34 and `GLIBCXX_3.4.29`, which is
satisfied by the
Ubuntu 22.04 / openEuler 24.03 base images used here.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Users of newly built A2/A3/A5 images get the FLA NPU
`26.10.0+feature`
kernels. No API or configuration change is required.

A release note fragment `release_notes/fragments/<PR number>.yaml`
should be
added with category `dependency` once the PR number is known.

### How was this patch tested?

- Verified that the Ascend mirror publishes the `26.10.0+feature` wheels
for
  A2, A3 and A5 on both `x86_64` and `aarch64`.
- Verified the changed Dockerfiles only bump `FLA_VERSION`; no install
logic or
  architecture detection is modified.
- `git diff --check` passes.

A full image build was not run locally because it requires the Ascend
CANN base
image and NPU build environment. The change is covered by the existing
image
build CI once triggered.

[Doc] Fix typos and casing in GLM documentation (#22211)

### What this PR does / why we need it?
This pull request cleans up the documentation for GLM-5.2,
GLM-5.3-Flash, and GLM-5 models by correcting casing, fixing typos and
standardizing link names.

Documentation changes do not require functional testing.

---

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [ ] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: I reviewed whether this change
involves
boundary conditions (e.g. empty input, single/zero element, min/max
values,
off-by-one, sequence-length limits, integer overflow). Where applicable,
I
added unit tests covering these edge cases in `tests/ut/` or
`tests/e2e/`.

test

- [ ] **Error / failure path coverage**: I covered abnormal paths
(exceptions,
timeouts, out-of-range, division by zero) in addition to the happy path.
- [ ] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: New tests assert real behavior
and are
  not written merely to satisfy CI.
- [ ] **Performance impact**: If this PR touches a performance-sensitive
path,
  I attached benchmark results and added performance regression tests.

[CI][Feature] Add Ascend recipe configuration checks (#20482)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

An Ascend recipe can pass schema validation while its effective
configuration still selects a NVIDIA image, offers a generic pip
installation, or generates inconsistent NPU arguments. This adds a
CPU-only configuration check after the existing official validator:

```text
Recipes / Validate
    └── Ascend configuration / Validate
```

The official reusable-workflow call remains unchanged. The dependent job
uses the official assembler, command generator and installation
resolvers to check:

- Effective Docker/pip settings and known NVIDIA/CUDA fallbacks.
- PD connector/router expectations, KV-transfer JSON and worker roles.
- Device-selection conflicts, invalid NPU IDs and single-node TP × DP ×
PP capacity.
- Known FlashInfer-only settings retained in Ascend commands.

Both standalone recipes under `models/` and fragments under `overlays/`
are checked after official assembly. Candidate and baseline use the same
renderer and source pins. **New or changed errors fail; existing errors
remain visible.** Source and zero-coverage failures always block.
JSON/Markdown reports are uploaded for configuration failures.

The local reusable workflow runs on `linux-amd64-cpu-4-hk`. It
initializes Node 22 before pnpm, avoiding the standalone pnpm binary's
missing `libatomic.so.1` dependency. The baseline is the tested merge's
first parent, so unrelated changes already on main are not attributed to
the PR.

Existing recipe values and the renderer repository are unchanged.
Details and coverage limits are documented in `recipes/tools/README.md`.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Recipe PRs gain a static configuration check and diagnostic artifact.
Inference behavior is unchanged.

Coverage includes Huawei standalone recipes and overlays with baseline
presets, optional features disabled and minimum multi-node topology.
Python frontend is requested, but inherited `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND` may
enable Rust. Registry availability, package/driver compatibility,
weights, NPU execution, performance and exhaustive topology/feature
combinations are outside this check. Existing configuration debt is
reported rather than certified as valid.

### How was this patch tested?

Revalidated with renderer `7565a964145bc7505197ab7d37e89db90493d1b5` and
recipes from main `f7b2118643268607d2fdcd8bf0230ce7282f881f`:

- **31 unit tests and 30 integration tests passed**, using the real
official assembler/generator. Three new regression tests failed before
the standalone-recipe fix and passed afterward.
- Regression coverage includes mixed and standalone-only sources, new
invalid-image failures, and existing baseline errors.
- JavaScript syntax/ESLint, actionlint, Markdown lint and `git diff
--check` passed.
- Current-main comparison: **16 models / 841 configurations, 0 new
errors / 0 blocking findings**. The report retains **1,589 existing
error findings**; this is not an all-configurations-pass claim.
- Upstream CI on `473de4a`: [official Recipes and Ascend configuration
validation](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/43861150207)
passed, including checker lint/tests and report upload. [Pre-commit and
both CPU unit-test
lanes](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/43861149759)
also passed.
- The remaining `ci-gate` failure is caused by missing CODEOWNERS
approvals, not failing code checks: workflow files require
`@zhangxinyuehfad`; `recipes/` files require `@SOMEONEUNSEEN`. No NPU
execution pass is claimed.

### Checklist

- [x] Boundary and regression cases covered.
- [x] Official assembler/generator exercised.
- [x] Current-main comparison completed with existing debt visible.
- [x] Fresh upstream recipe validation, pre-commit and CPU unit tests on
the latest commit.
- [ ] CODEOWNERS approvals.

- vLLM main:
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/ba15685ab7f4f5fbed8630bbb7441f8837e76fbe

@@ -0,0 +1,167 @@
+# Ascend recipe configuration checks
+
+These CPU-only checks run after the official renderer's recipe validation.
+The official reusable workflow retains ownership, schema and API validation; this
+tool checks effective Ascend installation and serving settings. It never
+executes recipe shell commands, pulls serving images, or loads model weights.
+
+## CI flow
+
+The original `validate` job keeps calling
+`vllm-project/recipes/.github/workflows/validate-recipes.yml@main` with its
+existing inputs. A separate `Ascend configuration` CPU job has `needs: validate`
+and calls the local `.github/workflows/_recipes_validate_ascend.yaml` reusable
+workflow only after the official check succeeds. The entry workflow contains
+only orchestration; checkout, setup, lint/tests, checks and upload live in the
+local reusable workflow. Changes to either workflow trigger the recipe check.
+No upstream changes or copies
+of the official workflow steps are needed in that original job.
+
+The additional job checks out the PR merge revision, target revision and
+`vllm-project/recipes@main`, installs its own renderer dependencies, then runs
+JavaScript syntax checks, ESLint, tests and Ascend configuration checks. Jobs
+do not share a filesystem: the downstream job prepares its own source cache.
+Within that job, candidate and baseline use the same renderer and source pins.
+The baseline is the merge revision's first parent, so changes already merged
+into the target branch are not mistaken for new errors from the PR.
+Both jobs independently resolve renderer main, so the report records the exact
+downstream SHA rather than claiming it must match the earlier job's SHA.
+Checkouts do not persist credentials, contents permission is read-only, and no
+NPU runner is requested.
+
+The checker invokes the renderer's `sync-sources.mjs` and strict
+`assemble-content.mjs` in temporary channels. Both candidate and baseline use
+the same non-Ascend source pins. Ambient `RECIPES_*` overrides are removed from
+child processes; source configuration is generated from the supplied renderer.
+Cleanup removes only these temporary channels, leaving `latest`, `validate`,
+the renderer's source configuration and public API output untouched.
+
+## Run locally
+
+Use Node.js 22 or later and a clean renderer checkout with its dependencies:
+
+```bash
+git clone https://github.com/vllm-project/recipes.git /tmp/recipes-renderer
+cd /tmp/recipes-renderer
+pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts
+cd /path/to/vllm-ascend
+node recipes/tools/validate-ascend.mjs \
+  --renderer /tmp/recipes-renderer \
+  --report /tmp/ascend-recipes/report.json
+```
+
+No manually prepared core YAML snapshot is required. The renderer fetches its
+locked recipe sources. `--recipes PATH` selects another Ascend recipe directory.
+Filters `--model org/model`, `--hardware ID`, `--variant KEY` and `--strategy KEY`
+can narrow a local investigation. No matching candidate configurations is a
+failure, not a successful empty scan. Symlink entries in inspected source trees
+are explicitly rejected rather than silently omitted.
+
+By default all errors block. To reproduce the PR's no-new-errors mode:
+
+```bash
+node recipes/tools/validate-ascend.mjs \
+  --renderer /tmp/recipes-renderer \
+  --baseline-recipes /path/to/target-revision/recipes \
+  --report /tmp/ascend-recipes/report.json
+```
+
+The baseline is checked with the current checker and the same renderer/source
+pins; it is not a committed findings allowlist. Findings are compared by model,
+hardware, variant, strategy, role, rule, severity, message and rule-specific
+evidence. New/changed errors block; unchanged errors stay visible as existing
+debt; removed errors are listed as resolved. Source/zero-coverage invariants
+always block. A missing or failed baseline cannot silently become a clean one.
+An empty valid baseline is allowed when adding the source's first model.
+
+Exit codes are `0` for no blocking findings, `1` for blocking findings, and `2`
+for input/tool failures. In no-new-errors mode, `0` does **not** mean all
+configurations are valid. `--warnings-as-errors` also blocks new warnings, or
+all warnings when no baseline is supplied.
+
+## Checks
+
+| Rule | Effective configuration checked |
+| --- | --- |
+| ASC001 | Empty/default GPU image, inherited NVIDIA/CUDA image map, or known NVIDIA image path. Custom NPU images need no particular registry or tag suffix. |
+| ASC002–003 | Visible pip tab using generic/CUDA defaults or explicitly selecting known CUDA wheel indexes. Adding dependencies does not replace the main pip installation command. |
+| ASC004–005 | Both installation methods disabled, or custom Docker setup directly pulling a known NVIDIA image. |
+| ASC010–014 | Missing PD expectations, connector/router mismatch, malformed KV JSON, or invalid producer/consumer role. NIXL is not banned by name. |
+| ASC020–023 | CUDA-only PD pinning; conflicting, duplicated, malformed or out-of-range device IDs; symbolic IDs reported as warnings. |
+| ASC024–025 | Single-node TP×DP×PP exceeding visible capacity, invalid parallel sizes, or symbolic sizes reported as warnings. TP/DP/PP aliases follow last-value precedence. |
+| ASC030 | Known FLASHINFER attention or MoE backend settings retained in NPU output. |
+
+Do not interpret this as a CUDA/NCCL word blacklist. Names such as
+`--gpu-memory-utilization`, `cudagraph_mode` and `NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME` are allowed.
+The device-range check assumes profile-local continuous numbering; explicit
+host/container remapping needs separate review.
+
+PD expectations may live at `recipes/validation/pd-expectations.json`, with
+each snapshot reading its own version. `--pd-expectations FILE` is an explicit
+local override. Entries have this shape:
+
+```json
+{
+  "example/model": {
+    "ascend_910c": {
+      "ascend_variant": {
+        "connector": "MooncakeConnectorV1",
+        "router": "vllm-router"
+      }
+    }
+  }
+}
+```
+
+The example shows the file structure, not a qualified deployment pairing.
+Expectations must describe the intended tutorial deployment; they are not
+runtime pass records. Do not change them solely to match an unintended default.
+
+## Compatibility and limits
+
+Installation checks reuse the renderer's exported `resolveInstall`,
+`hardwareInstall`, `hwPipOverride`, `isPipInstallAvailable` and
+`computeDockerMeta` helpers. This follows variant and hardware installation
+precedence without depending on JSX text fingerprints. Missing shared APIs
+fail with an actionable compatibility diagnostic; integration tests cover
+the effective installation and command/assembly behavior against renderer main.
+
+Coverage is Huawei standalone recipes and overlays, baseline preset, features disabled, Python
+frontend requested, default PD connector/router, and minimum multi-node topology.
+Inherited environment is preserved: `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1` may still enable
+Rust despite the Python request. Reports disclose this limitation; frontend
+compatibility is not verified. Full recipes under `models/` and fragments under
+`overlays/` use the same checks on their assembled configuration. Tuned presets, feature
+combinations, other frontends, all PD pool modes and all topology sizes are
+outside this change. Multi-node/PD per-node capacity is not verified.
+
+Custom install scripts and GPU-only package detection are not fully interpreted.
+The checker does not establish registry availability, package ABI compatibility,
+weight presence, NPU inference correctness or performance. Missing hardware
+opt-outs can expose extra page selections; those combinations are checked too.
+
+The official add-only migration rules remain in effect. If a core recipe still
+contains an imported Ascend field, conflicting downstream changes are rejected
+until the corresponding upstream split is completed.
+
+## Tests and reports
+
+```bash
+node --test recipes/tools/test-ascend-checks.mjs
+node recipes/tools/test-ascend-integration.mjs --renderer /tmp/recipes-renderer
+/tmp/recipes-renderer/node_modules/.bin/eslint \
+  --no-config-lookup --config recipes/tools/eslint.config.mjs recipes/tools/*.mjs
+```
+
+Integration tests use self-contained local fixtures and the real official
+assembler/generator, without remote source fetches. `--override source=PATH`
+is available for local non-Ascend source checkouts; it cannot replace the
+candidate Ascend source and is not used in CI.
+
+JSON and Markdown reports contain renderer/source provenance, input hashes,
+generated worker argv/env, findings and skipped combinations. The Actions
+summary shows at most 40 findings; the artifact contains the full report.
+Input/tool failures also write a failure report when `--report` is supplied.
+The workflow does not create or update branch-protection requirements. The
+existing reusable check is preserved; requiring the new Ascend check is a
+separate repository setting.

[BugFix][Scheduler] Preserve Mamba checkpoints in consumer chunked prefill (#21575)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

#### Overview

- **Branch:** `hechengkai:fix/mamba-consumer-prefill-checkpoints` →
`vllm-project:main`; an independent checkpoint fix discovered during
#21574 validation, after #20835 was merged.
- **Problem:** a KV consumer with a computed prefix bypasses Mamba/KDA
alignment even during ordinary chunked prefill, omitting a reusable
state checkpoint.
- **Reproduction:** recorded main `6d4f1c0`; prompt 2305, common cache
granularity 1152, expected reusable prefix `floor((2305 - 1) / 1152) *
1152 = 2304`. The budget limits each scheduling iteration, not cache
granularity.

| Prefill budget | External hit / expected | Consumer / no-pool
checkpoint boundary | Max absolute raw-logit error vs no-pool |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2048 | 1152 / 2304 | 1152 / 2304 | Cold: **1.03125** |
| 1024 | 2304 / 2304 | 2048 / 2304 | Reload: **8.4921875** |

- **Table interpretation:** requests reached token 2305, but missed
checkpoint 2304. A full external hit alone does not prove correct state
restoration; the 2048 case also diverged before reload.

- **Upstream contract:** Merged vLLM
[#51113](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51113) fixes
Mamba/GDN align-mode prefix-cache poisoning under EAGLE/MTP: a chunk-end
`state@364` could be published as `state@1600`. It extends prefill
alignment beyond `last_cache_position`, realigns mid-block resumes, and
retains `last_cache_position` as a mandatory snapshot stop. In
`mamba_cache_mode="align"`, the pinned [prefill
splitter](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/24420b7a341af37a9bc3186e6fc6062512e0aa58/vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py#L606-L660)
and [regression
tests](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/24420b7a341af37a9bc3186e6fc6062512e0aa58/tests/v1/core/test_mamba_align_chunk_split.py#L270-L319)
require cached states to match their advertised token boundaries. GLM
KDA uses this Mamba cache interface, so ordinary consumer prefills must
retain the required checkpoint stops.

#### Minimal change

- Keep the consumer/positive-prefix gate. Compute the remaining request
tokens from the request-computed, newly matched local, and external
prefix counts; ordinary prefill, including single-module MTP, continues
through checkpoint alignment.
- Preserve the complete window only when `num_new_tokens >
remaining_tokens` within the consumer/positive-prefix gate
(verifier/async placeholders), matching upstream
`_mamba_block_aligned_split` handling. Remove the method-name `is_mtp`
bypass.
- Reuse the existing alignment path: budget2048 changes chunks `[1152,
1153]` to `[1152, 1152, 1]`. No changes to lookahead reservation, cache

+    scheduler.add_request(request)
+    intervals: list[tuple[int, int]] = []
+    while request.num_computed_tokens < request.num_prompt_tokens:

+        assert end == start + count <= request.num_prompt_tokens

+            feedback = create_model_runner_output([request])
+            feedback.sampled_token_ids = [[]]
+            scheduler.update_from_output(output, feedback)

[Misc][Community] Update MLA attention and Kimi code owners (#22134)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Following the CODEOWNERS update in #21062, configure @hust17yixuan and
@Dawn952 as co-owners for these previously unclaimed MLA attention
backends:

- `/vllm_ascend/attention/flashmla.py`

All existing owners are preserved. The Kimi K3 directory entry covers
its model files, including those with additional file-specific owners
under the repository's cumulative ownership rules.

No. This only updates repository review ownership. No release note
fragment is needed.

- Validated all six entries with the repository's `codeowner_gate.py`
parser and owner resolution logic; both @Dawn952 and @hust17yixuan
resolve for every tracked file covered by these entries.

the diff contains exactly the requested ownership changes.

rebuilt revision.

then interrupted while the `actionlint` environment installation
remained pending; the full lint run did not complete.

No new tests or NPU testing are needed for this ownership metadata
change.

[Performance] Reuse head-first QKV storage in GDN prefill to eliminate redundant copies (#22010)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Supersedes #21739 and targets `main`.

The GDN prefill convolution can expose Q, K and V as sequence-first `[B,
T, H, D]` views of contiguous head-first `[B, H, T, D]` storage. The
base adaptor currently copies each tensor into sequence-first order,
then copies each back into head-first order for ChunkGDN. This round
trip costs six layout copies.

The adaptor converts each input to a head-first view and packs it only
if needed. Dense head-first inputs reuse their storage. A token slice
with gaps is packed directly in the layout ChunkGDN consumes. Q and K
are normalized over the same final dimension `D`.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Eligible prefill inputs automatically skip the six copies on the base
device adaptor. No configuration change is required.

### How was this patch tested?

The seven CPU-tensor layout tests were rerun on this port to `main`
(base `a1df499e0762`). The A3 hardware, serving and GPQA results below
were collected for the release-branch patch in #21739.

On A3, a 2,048-token prefill slice (17 leading tokens removed, 8 Q/K
heads, 24 V heads, head dimension 128, BF16) produced
elementwise-identical outputs and final recurrent states against the
previous PR head (`a04482cce`). Across 24 profiled calls per version,
the mean summed Q/K/V copy-kernel time fell from **110.04 to 24.46 µs**:
three AsStrided plus three Transpose kernels became three Slice kernels.
This measures layout copies for one sliced invocation.

A full AISBench GPQA Diamond rerun on the #21636 W4A8 integration stack
with the updated prefill function scored **179/198 (90.40%)**. The
previous layout implementation on that stack scored 183/198 (92.42%).
All 198 requests succeeded; two answers could not be extracted. This
single unseeded sampling run (32-way concurrency, 140,000-token output
cap) missed the 90.71% reference threshold by one correct answer. The
earlier three-run release-branch comparison below used a 120,000-token
cap.

#### Operator and serial-request performance

On Ascend A3 (W8A8, TP8, DP1), a rank-0 trace of a 16,435-token prefill
showed **6 → 0 QKV copy kernels in each of 180 GDN windows** across 36
layers, eliminating **20.37 ms of summed copy-kernel time** on that
rank. With profiling disabled, median TTFT for serial requests of the
same length fell from **2,278.90 to 2,245.56 ms (−1.46%)**, with 20
requests per variant.

#### Serving performance

We ran each workload once per variant on Ascend A3 with W4A8 weights,
using the same inputs and target request rate. A is the original
implementation and B enables the optimization. The table covers all
measured requests. Throughput and completed QPS changes are relative to
A.

| Input / output tokens | Requests per variant | Target req/s | Mean
TTFT, A → B (s) | Mean TPOT, A → B (ms/token) | Input / output
throughput change | Completed QPS change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 16K / 1 | 840 | 1.00 | 2.102 → 2.137 (+1.70%) | — | −0.02% / −0.02% |
−0.02% |
| 128K / 1 | 192 | 0.16 | 15.609 → 11.953 (−23.42%) | — | +0.63% /
+0.63% | +0.63% |
| End-to-end 16K / 1K | 660 | 1.00 | 2.205 → 2.240 (+1.61%) | 16.59 →
16.78 | +0.31% / +0.31% | +0.31% |
| End-to-end 128K / 1K, 90% shared prefix | 400 | 1.23 | 10.667 → 6.469
(−39.35%) | 16.63 → 16.55 | +1.65% / +1.65% | +1.65% |

Mean TTFT increased slightly in both 16K workloads. Shorter queues
accounted for most of the TTFT reduction at 128K. In the end-to-end 128K
/ 1K run, both variants had an **88.83% prefix-cache hit rate**. Mean
queue time on the prefill service fell from **6.482 to 2.336 s**, while
mean prefill execution time fell from **2.961 to 2.923 s**. Neither
end-to-end workload produced an AISBench steady-state window.

#### Numerical correctness and GPQA Diamond

All seven layout tests passed with CPU tensors (`python -m pytest -q -p
vllm_ascend.ops tests/ut/ops/test_gdn_layout.py`). In 11 numerical
comparisons on Ascend A3, Q, K, V, the GDN output and the final state
matched elementwise. Coverage included sequence lengths of 51, 63, 64,
65 and 4,096 tokens, non-contiguous token slices and continued state.
The hardware checks used release commit `62fe4cde69d9` with the layout
patch applied for variant B.

We evaluated Qwen3.8-Flash-Next W4A8 with AISBench through the
prefill/decode proxy. Only the prefill implementation changed. Each
variant answered the same 198 GPQA Diamond questions in three zero-shot
chain-of-thought runs, with B evaluated first. Both used
`temperature=1.0`, `top_p=0.95`, `top_k=20`, concurrency 32 and a
maximum output length of 120,000 tokens. No request-level sampling seed
was set.

| Run | A · original | B · optimized | B − A (percentage points) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 183/198 (92.42%) | 177/198 (89.39%) | −3.03 |
| 2 | 181/198 (91.41%) | 181/198 (91.41%) | 0.00 |
| 3 | 180/198 (90.91%) | 181/198 (91.41%) | +0.51 |
| **Mean accuracy** | **91.58%** | **90.74%** | **−0.84** |

B produced five fewer correct answers across the three runs. The per-run
differences varied in direction under stochastic decoding, so these
results alone cannot attribute the lower mean accuracy to the layout
change.

---

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [x] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: I reviewed whether this change
involves
boundary conditions (e.g. empty input, single/zero element, min/max
values,
off-by-one, sequence-length limits, integer overflow). Where applicable,
I
added unit tests covering these edge cases in `tests/ut/` or
`tests/e2e/`.
- [x] **Regression test**: If this PR fixes a bug, I added a regression
test
  that would fail without the fix.
- [ ] **Error / failure path coverage**: I covered abnormal paths
(exceptions,
timeouts, out-of-range, division by zero) in addition to the happy path.
- [x] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: New tests assert real behavior
and are
  not written merely to satisfy CI.
- [ ] **Performance impact**: If this PR touches a performance-sensitive
path,
  I attached benchmark results and added performance regression tests.

[CI][BugFix] Move review-event gate retrigger to a standalone workflow_run relay (#22221)

## What this PR does / why we need it?

Two real-PR failures exposed two independent holes in the ci-gate
review-retrigger design (`refresh_ci_gate.py`, #22106/#22133):

**1. Shadow skipped check allowed a merge through the gate (PR
#22202).**
`pr_test.yaml` previously triggered on both `pull_request` and
`pull_request_review`. A review-triggered E2E run skips `ci-gate` (its
`if` requires `pull_request`), but GitHub still creates a check-run for
the skipped job. Two check-runs then share the required `ci-gate`
context name on the head SHA, GitHub judges the required check by the
latest one, and a skipped check counts as satisfied — so the PR became
mergeable in the window before the real gate rewrote its verdict. #22202
merged (by its author) exactly through that window: merge at 14:28, gate
rewrite at 14:39.

**Fix:** move the retrigger out of `pr_test.yaml` entirely. The
`pull_request_review` trigger is deleted (with a comment forbidding its
return), and a standalone `pr_refresh_ci_gate.yaml` carries it. The
required `ci-gate` check now has exactly one producer, so a shadow
skipped verdict cannot exist.

**2. Fork-PR rescue failed with HTTP 403 (PR #22134).**
`GITHUB_TOKEN` is read-only for *every* workflow run tied to a fork PR,
regardless of the triggering event, and fork runs see no repository
secrets either — so `refresh_ci_gate.py`'s `rerun-failed-jobs` POST
always 403s for fork PRs, and the late-owner-approval rescue silently
degraded to a manual-rerun comment. This is the "fork PR actions:write"
risk item flagged as unverified when the retrigger landed; it is now
verified to fail.

**Fix:** split the retrigger into a two-hop relay:
- `pr_refresh_ci_gate.yaml` (`pull_request_review`, read-only token is
enough) only packages the review payload as an artifact;
- new `bot_ci_gate_refresh.yaml` (`workflow_run`, base repo context with
a writable token — the same safe pattern as the existing comment bot: it
never checks out or executes PR code, the script comes from the default
branch) downloads the payload and performs the actual re-run.

Also in this PR:
- `bot_ci_gate_comment.yaml` listens to the new `CI Gate Refresh`
workflow so the retrigger's own-failure comment contract still reaches
the PR;
- `pr_refresh_ci_gate.yaml` cancels a prior in-flight refresh per PR
(`cancel-in-progress: true`): with several reviews in quick succession,
the latest review wins; a cancelled relay loses nothing because the
script re-judges with live review state;
- `refresh_ci_gate.py`: no logic change, docstring only.

## Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No user-facing behavior changes for the happy paths (same-repo PRs
behave as before). Two observable changes:
- Fork PRs: a late owner approval now *actually* rescues the gate
(previously it 403'd and required a manual rerun, #22134).
- Review-event runs no longer produce a second, skipped `E2E / ci-gate`
check on the PR (the #22202 merge-bypass vector).

## How was this patch tested?

- `refresh_ci_gate.py` logic is unchanged: its 28 unit tests pass
unchanged (`pytest .github/workflows/scripts/test_refresh_ci_gate.py
--noconftest`).
- All touched workflow YAMLs parse cleanly (`yaml.safe_load`).
- `bash format.sh ci`: all hooks pass except the local gitleaks scan,
which fails for known local-environment reasons (no secrets in the diff;
CI will confirm).
- CI testing only for hardware/e2e aspects — no NPU behavior is touched.
- End-to-end behavior depends on `workflow_run` reading workflows from
the default branch, so it cannot be verified before merge. Post-merge
verification points:
1. fork PR + late owner approval → gate flips green automatically (the
#22134 scenario);
  2. same-repo PR rescue path unchanged;
  3. veto (CHANGES_REQUESTED / dismissed) still re-arms the gate red;
4. a review no longer creates a second, skipped `ci-gate` check on the
PR.

+# This file is a part of the vllm-ascend project.
+#
+
+name: CI Gate Refresh
+
+# Performs the ci-gate retrigger on behalf of pr_refresh_ci_gate.yaml
+# (pull_request_review). The review-event job cannot call the rerun API
+# itself: GITHUB_TOKEN is read-only for every run tied to a fork PR
+# regardless of the triggering event (#22134), and fork runs see no
+# repository secrets. `workflow_run` always executes in the base
+# repository context with a writable token, for same-repo and fork PRs
+# alike, so the actual re-run happens here.
+#
+# This workflow only reads the review-payload artifact produced by the
+# review-event job and talks to the GitHub API - it never checks out or
+# executes code from the PR, which keeps the write token out of reach of
+# untrusted input (the safe pull_request_target-style pattern; the script
+# comes from this repository's default branch, which a PR cannot alter).
+
+on:
+  workflow_run:
+    workflows:
+      - "Refresh CI Gate" # pr_refresh_ci_gate.yaml, the review-event relay
+    types:
+      - completed
+
+permissions:
+  actions: write # POST the rerun endpoints for the pull_request run
+  contents: read # checkout this repository's default branch for the script
+
+concurrency:
+  # Key by head SHA so retrigger runs for the same commit collapse into a
+  # single job: the script tolerates 409 conflicts and re-judges with live
+  # review state, so racing runs are redundant rather than harmful - but
+  # there is no point paying for two of them.
+  group: ci-gate-refresh-${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}
+  cancel-in-progress: true
+
+jobs:
+  rerun-gate-jobs:
+    # Only a completed relay run ships a payload; a cancelled relay (a newer
+    # review replaced it) is covered by the replacing run.
+    if: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success' }}
+    runs-on: linux-amd64-cpu-2-hk
+    # May wait for an in-flight pull_request CI run to finish before
+    # re-running its failed gate jobs (see refresh_ci_gate.py).
+    timeout-minutes: 360
+    steps:
+      - name: Download review payload
+        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          run-id: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
+          name: ci-gate-refresh-${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
+          github-token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
+          path: payload
+
+      - name: Export review payload as env
+        run: |
+          python3 - <<'PY' >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
+          import json
+
+          with open("payload/payload.json") as f:
+              payload = json.load(f)
+          for key, value in payload.items():
+              print(f"{key.upper()}={value}")
+          PY
+
+      - name: Checkout this repository's default branch
+        # The script must come from a tree the PR cannot alter (a PR must not
+        # be able to run its own gate logic); the default branch is the
+        # workflow_run checkout default, spelled out here for clarity.
+        uses: actions/checkout@v7
+        with:
+          persist-credentials: false
+
+      - name: Re-run the pull_request gate jobs
+        id: rerun
+        env:
+          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
+          # Maximum time (seconds) to wait for an in-flight pull_request CI
+          # run to complete before giving up.
+          GATE_WAIT_SECONDS: "7200"
+        run: |
+          # Rollout window only: until the PR that introduces this bot is
+          # itself merged, the script is not on the default branch yet and
+          # there is nothing to re-run with. Once merged this never triggers.
+          if [ ! -f ".github/workflows/scripts/refresh_ci_gate.py" ]; then
+            echo "::notice::refresh_ci_gate.py is not on the default branch yet; nothing to re-run."
+            exit 0
+          fi
+          python3 .github/workflows/scripts/refresh_ci_gate.py
+
+      - name: Package gate result
+        # Only this job's own failures (no CI run yet, wait timeout, rerun API
+        # error) need a PR comment; a successful retrigger hands the verdict
+        # back to the re-run pull_request run, whose own packaging step feeds
+        # the comment bot.
+        if: ${{ failure() }}
+        env:
+          CHECK_OUTCOME: ${{ steps.rerun.outcome }}
+        run: |
+          python3 - <<'PY'
+          import json
+          import os
+
+          result_dir = os.path.join(os.environ["RUNNER_TEMP"], "ci-gate-result")
+          os.makedirs(result_dir, exist_ok=True)
+          reason_file = os.path.join(
+              os.environ["RUNNER_TEMP"], "ci_gate_failure_reason.txt")
+          try:
+              with open(reason_file) as f:
+                  reason = f.read().strip()
+          except OSError:
+              reason = ""
+          result = {
+              "conclusion": os.environ["CHECK_OUTCOME"],
+              "reason": reason,
+              "pr": int(os.environ["PR_NUMBER"]),
+              "head_sha": os.environ["HEAD_SHA"],
+          }
+          with open(os.path.join(result_dir, "ci-gate-result.json"), "w") as f:
+              json.dump(result, f)
+          PY
+
+      - name: Upload gate result for the comment bot
+        # Same artifact contract as the ci-gate job: bot_ci_gate_comment.yml
+        # (workflow_run, base repo context) posts it to the PR.
+        if: ${{ failure() }}
+        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          name: ci-gate-result-${{ github.run_id }}
+          retention-days: 1
+          if-no-files-found: error
+          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/ci-gate-result/ci-gate-result.json

commits.message:
[Test][GDN] Guard the recurrent verify window against fla_npu pin bumps (#21936)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

`#16292` protected the legacy AscendC recurrent GDN kernel by adding a
local
per-sequence cap and a width gate in `vllm_ascend/ops/gdn.py`:

```python
_MAX_RECURRENT_GDN_TOKENS = 8
use_upstream_recurrent = ... or (
    spec_state_indices_tensor.ndim == 2 and spec_state_indices_tensor.shape[1] > _MAX_RECURRENT_GDN_TOKENS
)
```

That number describes the *installed fla_npu OPP*, not this repository.
Since
fla_npu `#1070` the arch22/arch35 kernel consumes a sequence in windows
and has
no per-sequence cap, but nothing connects the Python constant to the
kernel
that is actually installed. Two silent failures follow from a version
bump:

* bump fla_npu and leave the code alone → `k >= 8` keeps going to the
strided
  Triton kernel forever, with no error and no gain from the new kernel;
* delete the cap before the wheel ships it (or delete only half of it) →
a
  9-token window reaches the single-window kernel, which returns without
  writing output: the request produces garbage instead of an error.

This PR adds a CPU-only tripwire that reads the operator that is
installed and
fails when the code and the kernel disagree, naming the exact edit:

* classify the OPP from what the wheel installs: an `arch22/`/`arch35/`
directory means the window-loop kernel (no cap); otherwise the root
header's
`MAX_MTP = N` is the legacy fixed window. Vendors are visited in the
order
`opp/vendors/config.ini` declares, so an overlaid tree cannot describe
the
kernel that does not run. An unrecognised tree **fails** instead of
skipping,
  so a layout change cannot silently disable the guard.
* when `fla_npu` is not installed (e.g. a local environment), fall back
to the
version this repository pins, and require that version to be classified
in
  `KNOWN_OPP_WINDOWS` first.
* check the definition **and** its use site: with the window-loop kernel
both
`_MAX_RECURRENT_GDN_TOKENS` and the `spec_state_indices_tensor.shape[1]
> ...`
comparison must be gone (inlining `8` is caught); with the legacy kernel
the
constant must equal the header's `MAX_MTP` and the comparison must
reference
  it (deleting only the comparison is caught).
* the A2 `gdn_fixed_spec_recurrent_fallback_min_query_len = 9`
workaround is
tied to the same generation, since it was measured on the kernel that
the V2
  OPP replaced.

No production code changes. The existing cap stays until the fla_npu
release
containing `#1070` is pinned; at that point the test prints the removal
steps
and the follow-up patch applies them.

Reference: `#16292`, `#64427`.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. This PR only adds a unit test, plus one allowlisted word in
`typos.toml`
(the OPP vendor directory is literally named `tbe`); the released
artifact
behaves identically. Per `release_notes/README.md`, no release-note
fragment is
added because a user of the wheel or image cannot observe a difference.

### How was this patch tested?

CPU only, no device, no `fla_npu` import (`tests/ut/conftest.py`
replaces the
package with a stub, so the test locates the real distribution through
`importlib.metadata`).

Thirteen tests: three repository-state checks (pins agree and both kinds
of
file are seen, the pin is classified, the code matches the installed
kernel),
one scanner check (`==` and `===` are both recognised), eight detector
tests
(legacy 8, legacy 16, `arch22`, `arch35`, unknown layout, vendor order,
`config.ini` priority order, and the width comparison in its three
shapes) and
one self-check for an unclassified repository state.

Six combinations were exercised with the OPP swapped in place, against
the
current `main` sources (`vllm_ascend/ops/gdn.py` `1e6a9916`,
`vllm_ascend/device/hardware_profile.py` `4cc9a895`) and the
`flash-linear-attention-npu-a3==26.9.1` wheel that the CPU CI job
installs:

| OPP | code | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 26.9.1 (legacy) | unpatched | 13 passed |
| 26.9.1 (legacy) | cap removed (follow-up patch) | 1 failed — asks to
restore the cap |
| V2 (fla_npu main `5830fa6`) | cap removed | 13 passed |
| V2 | unpatched | 1 failed — asks to remove the cap |
| V2 | constant removed, `shape[1] > 8` inlined | 1 failed — reports the
inline comparison |
| 26.9.1 (legacy) | comparison removed, constant kept | 1 failed — asks
to restore the cap |

The follow-up patch was also checked against current `main` (`git apply
--check`): it still applies, with offsets only.

### Why not fix this in fla_npu?

`#1070` is already merged and fixes the kernel on `main`. The remaining
risk is
the hand-off in this repository (pin bump vs. code change), which only
this
repository can enforce. A capability API on the fla_npu side was
proposed but
is not being pursued.

### Notes

* The guard verifies routing, not numerics: it cannot prove that a
9-token
window produces correct output, only that it is no longer routed away
from
  the kernel or into a kernel that cannot handle it.
* Wide verify windows on `arch35` (A5) are not covered by on-device
tests yet;
  the guard would accept them as soon as the V2 wheel is pinned.

---

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [x] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: the guard pins the 8/9-token
boundary
  on both kernel generations — `MAX_MTP = 8` in the installed header vs.
`shape[1] > 8` in the dispatch — and the detector tests cover the legacy
8-token and 16-token headers, the `arch22`/`arch35` layouts, an unknown
  layout and vendor ordering.
- [x] **Regression test**: both silent failures a version bump can
produce are
covered — the kernel upgraded while the cap stays behind, and the cap
removed
while the legacy kernel is still installed (including the half-edit that
  deletes only the comparison or only the constant).
- [x] **Error / failure path coverage**: an unrecognised OPP tree fails
instead
of skipping, and the pin fallback fails when the pinned version is not
listed
  in `KNOWN_OPP_WINDOWS`.
- [x] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: the tests read the OPP that is
actually
installed (or the pins declared in this repository) instead of mocking a
  layout, and were exercised against six real code/OPP combinations.
- [ ] **Performance impact**: not applicable — a CPU-only unit test that
touches
  no performance-sensitive path.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+"""Keep the recurrent GDN dispatch in step with the installed fla_npu OPP.
+
+``vllm_ascend/ops/gdn.py`` carries a local per-sequence cap for the pre-V2
+AscendC recurrent kernel: that kernel consumed a single eight-token window and
+returned without writing output above it. ``fla_npu`` #1070 replaced it with an
+architecture-split, window-loop implementation that has no per-sequence cap.
+
+Nothing keeps the Python constant and the installed kernel in step: a fla_npu
+version bump changes the kernel silently, and the framework would keep routing
+wide verify windows to Triton. This test is that reminder. It reads the
+operator that is actually installed (or, when fla_npu is not installed, the
+version this repository pins) and fails when the two disagree, with the exact
+edit required. It checks the width comparison as well as the constant, since
+either half can reintroduce the cap on its own.
+
+The test runs no device code, so it is valid in the CPU unit-test job.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import importlib.metadata
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import regex as re
+
+REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
+GDN_SOURCE = REPO_ROOT / "vllm_ascend" / "ops" / "gdn.py"
+PROFILE_SOURCE = REPO_ROOT / "vllm_ascend" / "device" / "hardware_profile.py"
+OP_NAME = "recurrent_gated_delta_rule"
+
+# fla_npu version -> largest per-sequence verify window its OPP accepts.
+# ``None`` means the OPP is the window-loop kernel and imposes no cap.
+# Add an entry whenever the pins below move; ``test_declared_pins_agree``
+# fails until you do, which is the point of the guard.
+KNOWN_OPP_WINDOWS: dict[str, int | None] = {
+    "26.9.1": 8,
+}
+
+UNKNOWN = object()
+
+_MAX_MTP = re.compile(r"\bMAX_MTP\s*=\s*(\d+)\s*;")
+_CODE_CAP = re.compile(r"^_MAX_RECURRENT_GDN_TOKENS\s*=\s*(\d+)\s*$", re.MULTILINE)
+_CAP_NAME = "_MAX_RECURRENT_GDN_TOKENS"
+# The width gate #16292 added: ``spec_state_indices_tensor.shape[1] > 8``.
+# Match the use site as well as the definition. Deleting the constant but
+# inlining the number still caps the dispatch; deleting the gate but keeping
+# the constant sends wide windows to the capped kernel. Both are this bug.
+_WIDTH_GATE = re.compile(r"shape\[1\]\s*>\s*([A-Za-z_]\w*|\d+)")
+_PROFILE_OVERRIDE = re.compile(r"gdn_fixed_spec_recurrent_fallback_min_query_len\s*=\s*(\d+)")
+_DOCKER_PIN = re.compile(r'ARG\s+FLA_VERSION="([^"]+)"')
+_WORKFLOW_PIN = re.compile(r"flash-linear-attention-npu(?:-[^=\s\"]*)?==+\s*([0-9][\w.\-+]*)")
+
+REMOVE_THE_CAP = """\
+The installed fla_npu OPP is the window-loop kernel: {source} ships one
+directory per architecture and no fixed window, so it accepts any per-sequence
+verify length. vllm_ascend still caps the dispatch {limit}, which keeps
+k >= {threshold} on the Triton path forever.
+
+Delete both:
+  - vllm_ascend/ops/gdn.py: _MAX_RECURRENT_GDN_TOKENS and the whole
+    `spec_state_indices_tensor.shape[1] > ...` clause in
+    AscendGatedDeltaNetAttention._forward_core (do not inline the number)
+  - vllm_ascend/device/hardware_profile.py: the A2
+    gdn_fixed_spec_recurrent_fallback_min_query_len=9 workaround, which was
+    observed on the single-window kernel that this OPP replaced
+then update the guard branch in this test.
+"""
+
+RESTORE_THE_CAP = """\
+The installed fla_npu OPP still caps a sequence at {window} tokens ({source}),
+but vllm_ascend no longer caps the dispatch. On this pairing a verify window of
+{window_plus} tokens reaches the kernel, which returns without writing output:
+the request produces garbage instead of an error.
+
+Either install the fla_npu release that ships the window-loop kernel, or
+restore both _MAX_RECURRENT_GDN_TOKENS = {window} and its
+`spec_state_indices_tensor.shape[1] > _MAX_RECURRENT_GDN_TOKENS` clause in
+vllm_ascend/ops/gdn.py, plus the A2
+gdn_fixed_spec_recurrent_fallback_min_query_len workaround.
+"""
+
+UNKNOWN_LAYOUT = """\
+Cannot tell which recurrent GDN kernel is installed.
+
+The operator directory {where} has neither an architecture directory (V2
+window-loop kernel) nor a header carrying MAX_MTP (legacy fixed window). A
+fla_npu layout change has silently disabled this guard: inspect the installed
+tree and update the detector rather than skipping the test.
+"""
+
+
+def _ordered_vendors(vendors_root: Path) -> list[Path]:
+    """Vendor trees in the order the OPP loader visits them.
+
+    ``vendors/config.ini`` carries ``load_priority``; a wheel ships exactly one
+    vendor, so this only matters when a second tree has been overlaid.
+    """
+    priority: list[str] = []
+    config = vendors_root / "config.ini"
+    if config.is_file():
+        for line in config.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").splitlines():
+            key, _, value = line.partition("=")
+            if key.strip() == "load_priority":
+                priority = [name.strip() for name in value.split(",") if name.strip()]
+    rank = {name: index for index, name in enumerate(priority)}
+    vendors = [path for path in vendors_root.glob("*") if path.is_dir()]
+    return sorted(vendors, key=lambda path: (rank.get(path.name, len(rank)), path.name))
+
+
+def _installed_vendor_dirs() -> list[Path]:
+    """Vendor trees fla_npu installs, without importing the package.
+
+    ``tests/ut/conftest.py`` replaces ``fla_npu`` with a stub, so import it is
+    not an option here; the distribution metadata names the real tree.
+    """
+    roots: list[Path] = []
+    for dist in importlib.metadata.distributions():
+        name = (dist.metadata["Name"] or "").lower()
+        if name not in {"fla-npu", "fla_npu"} and not name.startswith("flash-linear-attention-npu"):
+            continue
+        package = Path(str(dist.locate_file("fla_npu")))
+        roots.extend(_ordered_vendors(package / "opp" / "vendors"))
+    return roots
+
+
+def _candidate_vendors() -> list[Path]:
+    """The installed vendor trees, in loader order.
+
+    Overlay trees are deliberately out of scope: the supported deployment is a
+    matching fla_npu wheel, and the guard must describe the kernel that wheel
+    installs. An unrecognised base tree fails instead of falling back.
+    """
+    return _installed_vendor_dirs()
+
+
+def _op_dirs(vendor: Path) -> list[Path]:
+    root = vendor / "op_impl" / "ai_core" / "tbe"
+    return sorted(path for path in root.glob(f"*/ascendc/{OP_NAME}") if path.is_dir())
+
+
+def _window_of(op_dir: Path) -> int | None | object:
+    # Check the architecture directories first: a V2 tree that still shipped a
+    # root header would otherwise be read as the legacy fixed window.
+    if (op_dir / "arch22").is_dir() or (op_dir / "arch35").is_dir():
+        return None
+    header = op_dir / f"{OP_NAME}.h"
+    if header.is_file():
+        match = _MAX_MTP.search(header.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"))
+        if match is not None:
+            return int(match.group(1))
+    return UNKNOWN
+
+
+def _installed_window() -> tuple[int | None | object, str]:
+    for vendor in _candidate_vendors():
+        op_dirs = _op_dirs(vendor)
+        if not op_dirs:
+            continue
+        # The vendor the loader visits first is the one whose kernel runs, so a
+        # lower-priority vendor cannot describe it.
+        return _window_of(op_dirs[0]), str(op_dirs[0])
+    return UNKNOWN, "no installed fla_npu OPP was found"
+
+
+def _declared_pins() -> dict[Path, str]:
+    pins: dict[Path, str] = {}
+    for path in sorted(REPO_ROOT.glob("Dockerfile*")):
+        if not path.is_file():
+            continue
+        for match in _DOCKER_PIN.finditer(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")):
+            pins[path] = match.group(1)
+    for path in sorted((REPO_ROOT / ".github" / "workflows").glob("*.y*ml")):
+        if not path.is_file():
+            continue
+        for match in _WORKFLOW_PIN.finditer(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")):
+            pins[path] = match.group(1)
+    return pins
+
+
+def _python_cap(source: Path = GDN_SOURCE) -> int | None:
+    match = _CODE_CAP.search(source.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
+    return None if match is None else int(match.group(1))
+
+
+def _width_gate(source: Path = GDN_SOURCE) -> str | None:
+    """What ``_forward_core`` compares the verify width against, if anything."""
+    match = _WIDTH_GATE.search(source.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
+    return None if match is None else match.group(1)
+
+
+def _profile_override() -> int | None:
+    match = _PROFILE_OVERRIDE.search(PROFILE_SOURCE.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
+    return None if match is None else int(match.group(1))
+
+
+def _declared_window() -> tuple[int | None | object, str]:
+    pins = _declared_pins()
+    if not pins:
+        return UNKNOWN, "no fla_npu pin was found in this repository"
+    versions = sorted(set(pins.values()))
+    if len(versions) > 1:
+        where = ", ".join(f"{path.relative_to(REPO_ROOT)}={version}" for path, version in pins.items())
+        return UNKNOWN, f"conflicting fla_npu pins: {where}"
+    version = versions[0]
+    if version not in KNOWN_OPP_WINDOWS:
+        return UNKNOWN, (
+            f"fla_npu {version} is not in KNOWN_OPP_WINDOWS; confirm whether that "
+            "release contains flash-linear-attention-npu #1070 and add the entry"
+        )
+    return KNOWN_OPP_WINDOWS[version], f"fla_npu {version}"
+
+
+def _observed_window() -> tuple[int | None | object, str]:
+    window, source = _installed_window()
+    if window is not UNKNOWN:
+        return window, source
+    # An installed but unrecognisable tree is a broken guard, not a reason to
+    # fall back to the pin: fail instead of pretending the pin describes it.
+    if _candidate_vendors():
+        return UNKNOWN, source
+    return _declared_window()
+
+
+def test_declared_pins_agree() -> None:
+    """Every place that pins fla_npu must name the same release."""
+    pins = _declared_pins()
+    # A scanner that silently stops matching one kind of file would let a
+    # disagreeing pin hide, so require both targets to be seen.
+    assert any(path.name.startswith("Dockerfile") for path in pins), "no Dockerfile pin was found"
+    assert any(path.suffix in {".yml", ".yaml"} for path in pins), "no workflow pin was found"
+    versions = sorted(set(pins.values()))
+    assert len(versions) <= 1, f"fla_npu pins disagree: {versions}"
+
+
+def test_workflow_pin_accepts_both_specifiers() -> None:
+    """``==`` and ``===`` both pin; missing either would hide a workflow."""
+    cases = {
+        "uv pip install --no-deps flash-linear-attention-npu-a3===26.9.1": "26.9.1",
+        "uv pip install --no-deps flash-linear-attention-npu-a3==26.9.1": "26.9.1",
+        "flash-linear-attention-npu==26.10.0": "26.10.0",
+    }
+    for line, expected in cases.items():
+        match = _WORKFLOW_PIN.search(line)
+        assert match is not None, line
+        assert match.group(1) == expected, line
+
+
+def test_declared_window_is_known() -> None:
+    """A pin bump must classify the release before anything else can run."""
+    window, source = _declared_window()
+    assert window is not UNKNOWN, source
+
+
+def test_dispatch_cap_matches_installed_kernel() -> None:
+    """The Python cap must describe the kernel that is actually installed."""
+    window, source = _observed_window()
+    assert window is not UNKNOWN, (
+        source if "fla_npu" in source and "not in KNOWN" in source else UNKNOWN_LAYOUT.format(where=source)
+    )
+
+    cap = _python_cap()
+    gate = _width_gate()
+    if window is None:
+        limit = f"at {cap} tokens" if cap is not None else f"with `shape[1] > {gate}`"
+        message = REMOVE_THE_CAP.format(source=source, limit=limit, threshold=cap if cap is not None else gate)
+        assert cap is None, message
+        assert gate is None, message
+        assert _profile_override() is None, message
+        return
+
+    if not isinstance(window, int):
+        raise AssertionError(UNKNOWN_LAYOUT.format(where=source))
+
+    assert cap == window, RESTORE_THE_CAP.format(window=window, source=source, window_plus=window + 1)
+    # Deleting the gate while keeping the constant would send wide windows to
+    # the capped kernel with nothing left to stop them.
+    assert gate == _CAP_NAME, RESTORE_THE_CAP.format(window=window, source=source, window_plus=window + 1)
+    # The numerical workaround belongs to the single-window kernel; it must
+    # stay while that kernel is the one installed.
+    assert _profile_override() is not None, RESTORE_THE_CAP.format(window=window, source=source, window_plus=window + 1)
+
+
+class TestDetector:
+    """The detector itself, so a layout change fails here first."""
+
+    def test_legacy_window_is_read_from_the_kernel_header(self, tmp_path: Path) -> None:
+        op_dir = tmp_path / "op"
+        op_dir.mkdir()
+        (op_dir / f"{OP_NAME}.h").write_text("constexpr uint64_t MAX_MTP = 8;\n", encoding="utf-8")
+        assert _window_of(op_dir) == 8
+
+    def test_a_wider_legacy_window_is_not_hard_coded(self, tmp_path: Path) -> None:
+        op_dir = tmp_path / "op"
+        op_dir.mkdir()
+        (op_dir / f"{OP_NAME}.h").write_text("constexpr uint64_t MAX_MTP = 16;\n", encoding="utf-8")
+        assert _window_of(op_dir) == 16
+
+    def test_architecture_directory_means_no_cap(self, tmp_path: Path) -> None:
+        op_dir = tmp_path / "op"
+        (op_dir / "arch22").mkdir(parents=True)
+        # A V2 tree that still shipped the dead header must still read as V2.
+        (op_dir / f"{OP_NAME}.h").write_text("constexpr uint64_t MAX_MTP = 8;\n", encoding="utf-8")
+        assert _window_of(op_dir) is None
+
+    def test_arch35_alone_is_the_same_v2_kernel(self, tmp_path: Path) -> None:
+        op_dir = tmp_path / "op"
+        (op_dir / "arch35").mkdir(parents=True)
+        assert _window_of(op_dir) is None
+
+    def test_unrecognised_layout_is_unknown(self, tmp_path: Path) -> None:
+        op_dir = tmp_path / "op"
+        op_dir.mkdir()
+        (op_dir / "something_else.h").write_text("// nothing\n", encoding="utf-8")
+        assert _window_of(op_dir) is UNKNOWN
+
+    def test_first_vendor_that_ships_the_operator_decides(self, tmp_path: Path) -> None:
+        legacy = tmp_path / "legacy" / "op_impl" / "ai_core" / "tbe" / "impl" / "ascendc" / OP_NAME
+        legacy.mkdir(parents=True)
+        (legacy / f"{OP_NAME}.h").write_text("constexpr uint64_t MAX_MTP = 8;\n", encoding="utf-8")
+        v2 = tmp_path / "v2" / "op_impl" / "ai_core" / "tbe" / "impl" / "ascendc" / OP_NAME
+        (v2 / "arch22").mkdir(parents=True)
+
+        assert _op_dirs(tmp_path / "legacy") == [legacy]
+        assert _window_of(_op_dirs(tmp_path / "legacy")[0]) == 8
+        assert _window_of(_op_dirs(tmp_path / "v2")[0]) is None
+
+    def test_vendor_order_follows_the_packaged_config(self, tmp_path: Path) -> None:
+        vendors = tmp_path / "vendors"
+        for name in ("aaa", "mmm", "zzz"):
+            (vendors / name).mkdir(parents=True)
+        (vendors / "config.ini").write_text("load_priority=zzz,aaa\n", encoding="utf-8")
+        assert [path.name for path in _ordered_vendors(vendors)] == ["zzz", "aaa", "mmm"]
+
+        (vendors / "config.ini").unlink()
+        assert [path.name for path in _ordered_vendors(vendors)] == ["aaa", "mmm", "zzz"]
+
+    def test_width_gate_reports_the_comparison_operand(self, tmp_path: Path) -> None:
+        source = tmp_path / "gdn.py"
+        source.write_text(
+            "use_upstream_recurrent = flag or (\n"
+            "    indices.ndim == 2 and indices.shape[1] > _MAX_RECURRENT_GDN_TOKENS\n"
+            ")\n",
+            encoding="utf-8",
+        )
+        assert _width_gate(source) == _CAP_NAME
+
+        source.write_text("use_upstream_recurrent = flag or (indices.shape[1] > 8)\n", encoding="utf-8")
+        assert _width_gate(source) == "8"
+
+        source.write_text("use_upstream_recurrent = flag\n", encoding="utf-8")
+        assert _width_gate(source) is None
+
+
+def test_repository_state_is_classified() -> None:
+    """This repository's own sources must match one of the known states."""
+    cap = _python_cap()
+    assert cap in (None, 8), (
+        "The dispatch cap was changed without updating this guard; record the new "
+        "state in KNOWN_OPP_WINDOWS and the assertions above."
+    )

[Attention][Feature] Support TP × PCP KDA sharding for GLM-5.3-Flash (#21510)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR enables joint Tensor Parallelism (TP) and Prefill Context
Parallelism (PCP) head sharding for the KDA layer in GLM-5.3-Flash.
Previously, PCP participated in KDA head sharding only when TP was 1.
Projections, convolution weights, and recurrent state are now sharded
across TP × PCP ranks in TP-major order, matching Mooncake V2 state
transfer. The output projection combines PCP contributions before the
optional TP reduction so the sequence-parallel decoder can still defer
TP reduction.

RecoverSSM now accepts TP > 1 with PCP > 1 on KV producers. Its records
use the same local head count as the projections and recurrent state.
PCP consumers and colocated PCP execution remain unsupported; the
speculative-decoding, PP=1, DCP=1, cache-mode, and stochastic-rounding
checks remain in place.

Follows the KDA sharding approach in #21017.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Native KDA and RecoverSSM prefill producers support joint TP × PCP
head sharding. The KDA head count must be divisible by TP × PCP. The
RecoverSSM documentation and release note describe the supported
configuration.

### How was this patch tested?

**2026-11-17 conflict/CPU-UT update (`ec722e555`):**

- The two failed CPU jobs in run
[43708732339](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/43708732339)
stopped during `git rebase`, before pytest. Rebased the feature onto
main `915d58873`, resolved the KDA/input-projection-TP conflicts, and
preserved the RecoverSSM and PCP reduce-scatter changes previously
carried by merge commits. Repeating the CI rebase command succeeds.
- Explicit `tp_group` projections retain their own shard rank/size and
collectives; default projections compose TP x PCP. Added
weight-loader/collective regression coverage with nontrivial default TP
and PCP groups; retained main's input-projection and static-bias
coverage.
- Linux CPU-only container, no NPU devices, real pytest with the
repository CPU mocks: **385 passed** on each of vLLM verified main
`ba15685ab7f4f5fbed8630bbb7441f8837e76fbe` and `v0.33.0`. Tested
`test_glm5next_kda_{pcp,dispatch,reduce_scatter,input_projection_tp,contracts,state_dtype}.py`
and `test_glm5next_recoverssm_config.py` under `tests/ut/models/`.
- Ruff check/format, Markdown lint, codespell, typos, forbidden-import,
boolean-context-manager, long-function and diff-whitespace checks
passed. `bash format.sh ci` was attempted on Windows but stalled
installing the actionlint Go environment; the complete check remains
covered by [CI run
44009645674](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/44009645674).
- No new NPU benchmark was run for this conflict repair. The original
native-KDA hardware results below remain evidence for `28666d61d`, not a
benchmark of the rebased head; RecoverSSM multi-card hardware validation
remains pending.

Validated on A3 with MRV2 and GLM-5.3-Flash W8A8C8 using PD separation
on one host: eight logical NPU devices for Prefill **TP2/PCP4** and
eight for Decode **TP8/PCP1/DCP1**. Prefill uses eager mode; Decode uses
`FULL_DECODE_ONLY`. `enable_pcp_o_proj_weight_sharding=true` in both
arms.

Baseline: main `faa43c37d` **plus a GLM KDA/Mamba state-transfer fix**
that infers head shards and PCP replicas from cache shapes and copies
the corresponding head slices for this PD topology. Candidate: this PR
at `28666d61d`, without that local baseline patch. Both use vLLM
`24420b7a34`.

Completed three rounds of all **198 GPQA Diamond questions per version**
on 2026-11-16, with `max_tokens=65536`, `reasoning_effort=low`,
temperature 1, top_p 0.95, seed 1024 and client concurrency 100. Each
branch reuses one service startup for its three rounds, with five smoke
requests and a 100-request concurrency probe before measurement;
requests are drained and prefix caches reset between rounds. Decode
graph replay and actual concurrency 100 were verified for both services.
Mean results across all three rounds:

| Metric | Baseline (main + transport fix) | Candidate (this PR) |
Candidate change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| GPQA strict accuracy | 71.21% (423/594) | 73.06% (434/594) | +1.85
percentage points |
| Mean TTFT | 4.211 s | 3.663 s | 13.00% lower |
| Mean TPOT | 56.662 ms/token | 56.857 ms/token | 0.34% higher |
| Prefill model-loading allocation | 42.36 GiB/rank | 39.12 GiB/rank |
3.24 GiB/rank lower |
| Decode model-loading allocation | 38.59 GiB/rank | 38.59 GiB/rank |
Unchanged |

Completed **1,188/1,188 measured requests with zero request errors**.
The 64K output limit truncated 8 baseline responses and 9 candidate
responses; these count as incorrect. Strict scoring requires a final
`Answer: A-D` on normal completion; missing or unrecognized final
answers also count as incorrect. The denominator is 198 questions
repeated three times per version. TTFT includes the first streamed
reasoning/text token; TPOT is averaged per request. Weight figures are
model-loading allocations, not total HBM usage; the 3.24 GiB/rank
reduction is the branch difference with o_proj sharding enabled in both
arms.

Both versions have higher TTFT in their first round. Across rounds 2-3
with the same services reused, mean TTFT is 2.332 s for the baseline and
1.822 s for this PR (21.88% lower); mean TPOT is 56.766 versus 56.980
ms/token. The table above includes all three rounds.

<details>
<summary>Six-round GPQA results</summary>

| Version | Round | Strict accuracy | Mean TTFT (s) | Mean TPOT
(ms/token) | 64K truncations |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| main + transport fix | 1 | 72.22% (143/198) | 7.969 | 56.454 | 3 |
| main + transport fix | 2 | 71.72% (142/198) | 2.334 | 56.730 | 2 |
| main + transport fix | 3 | 69.70% (138/198) | 2.329 | 56.802 | 3 |
| This PR | 1 | 71.72% (142/198) | 7.346 | 56.611 | 2 |
| This PR | 2 | 73.23% (145/198) | 1.843 | 57.200 | 3 |
| This PR | 3 | 74.24% (147/198) | 1.800 | 56.759 | 4 |

All 1,188 per-request records were checked against the round summaries.
These hardware runs cover the native KDA path; multi-card RecoverSSM
validation remains outstanding.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Existing CPU/static checks and remaining RecoverSSM
validation</summary>

- Extended `test_glm5next_recoverssm_config.py` for TP1/PCP8, TP2/PCP4,
and TP4/PCP2 producers, both Mooncake transfer connectors, prefix
caching, and eager/graph settings. Added TP > 1 Store coverage and
retained rejection of missing transfer configuration, PCP consumers, and
`kv_both` roles.
- Updated `test_glm5next_kda_pcp.py` to use the actual RecoverSSM
configuration switch and validator. The construction cases check joint
projection/state sharding and RecoverSSM record shapes across the graph
modes.
- Local standalone CPU checks of the production configuration validator
passed: 48 valid configurations and 15 rejected configurations. All 32
TP > 1 / PCP > 1 positive cases reproduced the original TP=1 rejection
before the fix and passed after it. These checks do not execute NPU
kernels, distributed collectives, or pydantic initialization.
- Python compilation and `git diff --check origin/main` passed. Ruff
check/format, codespell, and Markdown lint passed.
- Full `bash format.sh ci` was attempted. Actionlint environment
installation stalled; a retry excluding actionlint reached the remaining
hooks. Some hooks could not complete on this Windows host because of
missing shellcheck, `/bin/bash` or `python3` launchers, and the
full-tree typos scan exhausted memory. These environment-dependent
checks still require CI.
- Full pytest collection could not start locally (`ModuleNotFoundError:
vllm`); the Ascend runtime is also unavailable. Run the following
regression files in the supported CI environment, followed by multi-card
RecoverSSM validation with TP2/PCP4 and TP4/PCP2 producers:

  ```shell
  pytest -q tests/ut/models/test_glm5next_recoverssm_config.py \
    tests/ut/models/test_glm5next_kda_pcp.py \
    tests/ut/models/test_glm5next_kda_dispatch.py \
    tests/ut/models/test_glm5next_kda_reduce_scatter.py
  ```

</details>

[Misc] Add Ronald1995 as codeowner for common RLHF e2e tests (#22186)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Add `/tests/e2e/common/rlhf/ @Ronald1995` in the existing tests section
of CODEOWNERS. The repository's ownership gate inherits `@wenjun91` from
`/tests/`, so the RLHF rule lists only the additional owner.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. Repository ownership metadata only; no release note fragment is
needed.

### How was this patch tested?

- Checked the revised CODEOWNERS with the repository's own parser
against every tracked file: all **9 common RLHF files** inherit
`@wenjun91` from `/tests/` and add `@Ronald1995`, all **26 PR RLHF
files** retain their ownership exemption, and ownership for all other
files is unchanged.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- Existing CODEOWNERS parser/gate tests passed earlier in this PR: **56
passed**.
- The earlier full `bash format.sh ci` run encountered Windows
environment limitations (missing `/bin/bash`, ShellCheck and a working
`python3` for several hooks); png-lint also reported failure, with no
remaining tracked image changes. Full lint validation remains for CI.
- No runtime tests added or NPU tests run because this change only
updates ownership metadata.

---

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [ ] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: Not applicable; metadata only.
- [ ] **Regression test**: Not applicable; no runtime bug fix.
- [ ] **Error / failure path coverage**: Not applicable; metadata only.
- [x] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: Existing CODEOWNERS tests and
focused ownership checks passed.
- [ ] **Performance impact**: Not applicable; no runtime changes.

- vLLM main:
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/ba15685ab7f4f5fbed8630bbb7441f8837e76fbe

---------

Signed-off-by: Ronald1995 <ronaldautomobile@163.com>
